status: PARTIAL — harvested while the run was still in its verify phase

finders.lens: Declared in a schema/config and consumed by nothing — every field, column, and vocabulary term in `/schema/*.json`, `server/src/db/migrations/*.sql`, and the import config snapshot, traced to a reader.

findings.title: Every `record-set` slot in the binder schema is structurally incapable of producing a gap, because the four schema keys that define a record-set's expectation — `recordFields`, `completeWhen`, `expectationSource`, `keyedBy` — have zero readers anywhere in the repo.
findings.why_it_matters: Five of the profile's `required` slots are record-sets: `s7.components`, `s10.findings`, `s10.concerns`, `s11.warranties`, `s13.tests` (schema/profiles/baseline-v1.json:8-40). Trace each through `assessSlot`: `s11.warranties` sources only `documents`, which has no reader, so `unwiredNote` fires and it correctly reports `empty` with its reason. The other four do not. `s10.findings` and `s13.tests` name a `field.*` source, which IS wired, so `unwiredNote` returns undefined (sources.ts:124-134), the record-set branch runs, `slot.id !== 's7.components'` yields `expected: 0`, and completeness.ts:365 turns that into **`state: 'complete'`**. `s10.concerns` declares no `sources` key at all, so `sources ?? []` is empty, `unwiredNote` returns undefined at its first guard, and it lands on the same path. `s7.components` sets `withRecord = expected` by construction, so it is `complete` when pins exist and `complete` with `expected: 0` when they do not — on a Discovery export, which migration 022 says produces zero pins by design, the house's Systems inventory reports complete. `gapList` (completeness.ts:425) filters `state !== 'complete'`, so none of the four can ever reach the gap report. The Increment 3 build spec defines the kind as "Every entity in the expectation set has a record, and each record satisfies its required fields" — neither half is implemented, and the schema keys that carry both halves have no reader. CLAUDE.md §15 records that concerns and lab results are unbuilt; the audit does not report them as unbuilt, it reports them as done. This is Verification Discipline rule 11 exactly: the only record-set that exercises the `expected` vs `withRecord` comparison is the one where the two sides are the same number.
findings.falsifiable_as: Run `runAudit` against any property, from any fixture, and inspect the returned slots. If this is real you will see `s10.concerns`, `s10.findings` and `s13.tests` come back with `state: 'complete'`, `required: true`, `detail: { expected: 0 }`, `missing: []`, and none of them present in `result.gaps` — on a database where no concern, no finding record and no test result exists. `s7.components` will come back `complete` on a pin-free import with `detail.expected === 0`. It would be disproved if any of those four appears in `result.gaps`, or if some caller reads `recordFields`/`completeWhen`/`expectationSource` to build a real expectation set — `grep -rn "recordFields\|completeWhen\|keyedBy" server web --include=*.ts` returning a non-comment hit would disprove it.

findings.title: `neverAI` and `aiMayDraft` — doctrine 9's "Never AI" list, written into the binder schema as machine-readable flags on six slots and fields — have no reader anywhere in the repository.
findings.evidence:
The declarations:
  schema/binder-schema-v1.json:609  "id": "planning-horizon", "source": "human", "neverAI": true
  schema/binder-schema-v1.json:614  "id": "replacement-allowance", "source": "human", "neverAI": true,
                                    "rule": "A planning window, never a quote and never a date."
  schema/binder-schema-v1.json:878  "aiMayDraft": ["what-was-observed", "why-it-matters"]
  schema/binder-schema-v1.json:882  "neverAI": ["urgency", "planning-cost-range", "recommended-action"]
  schema/binder-schema-v1.json:1118 "id": "s19.reserve-figure", ... "neverAI": true
  schema/binder-schema-v1.json:555,561,567,573  "requiresHumanAccept": true  (make, model, serial, fuel-capacity)

The search for a reader:
  $ grep -rn "neverAI\|aiMayDraft\|requiresHumanAccept\|never_ai" . \
      --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx --include=*.sql --include=*.js --include=*.yml | wc -l
  0

The nearest thing to enforcement reads a different key entirely — renderGate.ts:118 reads `slot.outsideHonestyVocabulary`, never `neverAI`, and s19.reserve-figure declares both.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the failure `server/src/report/renderGate.ts:19-24` names in its own header and then does not generalise: *"The obvious build is a `renderNote` on the slot that a renderer may emit. **That is Table I** — `audit/provenance.ts`, five exported functions built, tested, and called by nothing... An optional field is satisfied by declaring it; the failure it exists to prevent survives untouched."* `neverAI` is that shape precisely. The `requiresHumanAccept` half happens to be covered by accident — `ai/accept.ts` makes human acceptance universal for every generation, so nameplate fields cannot bypass a signature whether or not the flag is read. There is no equivalent universal mechanism for `neverAI`: nothing anywhere refuses to route `s19.reserve-figure`, `urgency`, `planning-cost-range`, `recommended-action`, `planning-horizon` or `replacement-allowance` to a model. Today the consequence is latent rather than active — no binder-section renderer exists and no AI task writes into an s7 record field or an s10 concern field, so no value can currently reach one of these. But `docs/…Property-Flags-and-Session-Plan_Code-Reply_2026-08-07.md:136` already describes a render check that treats `neverAI` and `classD_irreduciblyHuman` as hard refusals, and neither key is read. The wall is written down where a future author will read it as already enforced.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real, `grep -rn "neverAI" --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx --include=*.sql .` returns nothing, and constructing a `Slot` object for `s19.reserve-figure` and passing an AI-produced string to every exported function in `server/src/report/` and `server/src/ai/` produces no refusal citing `neverAI`. It would be disproved by any code path — a doctrine scan, a prompt router, a render gate — that reads the key or refuses on it. Note the honest limit: because no binder renderer exists, you cannot today demonstrate an AI-authored reserve figure actually reaching a page; the claim is that the declared wall has no enforcement point, not that a value is currently crossing it.

findings.title: `product_resolutions.honesty` is written on every row and read by nothing, so the `Inferred` label the migration says must travel with the row does not travel.
findings.evidence:
The column, and the migration's stated reason for it:
  024_product_resolutions.sql:65-67
    -- Only ever `Inferred` in this build. The column exists so the value travels
    -- with the row rather than being reconstructed by whoever renders it.
    honesty       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Inferred',

The write, as a SQL literal, on every resolution row:
  server/src/ai/tasks/resolveProduct.ts:324-327
    `INSERT INTO product_resolutions
       (id, property_id, import_id, reading_id, query, specificity, resolved, product, kind,
        recognised_from, honesty, generation_id, actor_id, created_at)
     VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 'Inferred', ?, ?, ?)`

Every read of the table, and none of them names the column:
  resolveProduct.ts:185  SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM product_resolutions WHERE import_id = ?
  resolveProduct.ts:356  SELECT p.product, p.kind, p.specificity, p.reading_id, r.media_id FROM product_resolutions p JOIN readings r ...
  matchComplete.ts:729   SELECT p.product, p.id FROM product_resolutions p WHERE p.import_id = ? AND p.resolved = 1
  scripts/passes.ts:195  SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM product_resolutions WHERE import_id = ? AND resolved = 1
  scripts/resolve.ts:158 SELECT resolved, product, kind, specificity, recognised_from AS why, query FROM product_resolutions ...

  $ grep -rn "honesty" server/src server/scripts web/src --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx | grep -i select | wc -l
  0
findings.why_it_matters: Doctrine 2 — honesty labels survive the pipeline — is the rule this column exists to serve, and the column is the seam where it stops. Pass 2's resolution feeds pass 3 (`matchComplete.ts:729` reads `product` and `id`), which writes an object with `derived_from = 'plate'` and `resolution_id`. `objects` has no honesty column (017_objects.sql, 025_object_lanes.sql, 026_object_model_read.sql), so the `Inferred` claim is recorded once and dropped at the first join. The migration's own defence — that the value should travel rather than be reconstructed by a renderer — is the argument for a reader, and there is no reader; a renderer added later will reconstruct it, which is the thing the column was written to prevent. This is not the deliberate wall in the same migration: the wall is the *absence* of a `source_url` column so that `Documented` is unreachable, and that is correct and untouched here. This is a column that exists, is written, and is never read.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real, `grep -rn "honesty" server/src server/scripts web/src --include=*.ts` shows exactly one SQL occurrence — the INSERT column list at resolveProduct.ts:326 — and no SELECT anywhere names it; and after a pass-2 run, `SELECT honesty FROM product_resolutions` holds `Inferred` on rows whose derived objects carry no honesty label at all. It would be disproved by any query, script output, or API response that reads the column back.

findings.title: The import config snapshot's `provenance[]` array — Table I, eight declared derived items — is read only by `audit/provenance.ts`, whose five exported functions are called by nothing but their own test file.
findings.evidence:
The only consumer of the declared array:
  server/src/audit/provenance.ts:62  * Table I, from `config.snapshot.provenance`.
  server/src/audit/provenance.ts:81  export function provenanceMap(snapshot: Record<string, unknown>): Map<string, ProvenanceRow> {
  server/src/audit/provenance.ts:83    const declared = snapshot.provenance

Who imports that module:
  $ grep -rn "audit/provenance" server/src server/scripts web/src server/test --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx
  server/src/report/renderGate.ts:20:  * **That is Table I** — `audit/provenance.ts`, five exported functions built,
  server/test/provenance.test.ts:25:} from '../src/audit/provenance.js'

The five exports, all unreachable from production:
  provenance.ts:38  export type Verification = 'verified' | 'unverifiable' | 'unknown-provenance'
  provenance.ts:81  export function provenanceMap(...)
  provenance.ts:126 export function verify(args: VerifyArgs): VerifiedValue
  provenance.ts:214 export function aggregate(values: VerifiedValue[]): ProvenanceBreakdown
  provenance.ts:234 export const mergeBreakdowns = ...
  provenance.ts:249 export function describeProvenance(b: ProvenanceBreakdown): string[]

What the config declares and nothing reaches (walk fixture, config v1.11.0):
  { "itemId": "wh.age",  "derivedFrom": "Serial number, manufacturer-decoded", "sourceItemId": "wh.nameplate" }
  { "itemId": "pnl.service", "derivedFrom": "Main breaker amp marking / rating label", "sourceItemId": "pnl.label" }
  ... 8 rows in total
findings.why_it_matters: The schema states the rule this module implements: `binder-schema-v1.json`'s `tableI_provenance` — *"any value transcribed from a physical artifact names the photo item that captures it. **The builder must carry the declaration, not just the value.** A value whose source photo item resolved `na / none-present` is **unverifiable** and must stay distinguishable from a verified one at every layer."* The three-state `Verification` type is Verification Discipline rule 6's own worked example — *verified / unverifiable / unknown-provenance*, where collapsing to two states reports the unknown case as the safe one. All three states are computed and none is reachable, so no audit run, no gap report, no session plan and no screen distinguishes a transcribed value whose source photo was never captured from one whose source photo is on file. `renderGate.ts:20` cites this module by name as the cautionary example for why *its* design had to be a gate rather than an optional field — the lesson was drawn and the instance is still live, and `tableI_provenance` plus `config.snapshot.provenance` are declared config with no path to a reader.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real, `grep -rn "provenanceMap\|describeProvenance\|mergeBreakdowns" server/src server/scripts web/src` returns only the definitions inside `audit/provenance.ts` itself, and importing an export whose config declares all eight Table I rows produces an audit run, gap report and session plan in which no field distinguishes verified from unverifiable. It would be disproved by any production import of `audit/provenance.js`, or by a `Verification` value appearing in an API response or rendered document.

findings.title: The `object_states` table and every function that gives its vocabulary consequence — `suppressesCare`, `blocksOperation`, `doNotOperateLine` — have no production writer and no production reader; only tests touch either.
findings.evidence:
The table, with seven columns and a full open vocabulary:
  023_operating_state.sql:46  CREATE TABLE object_states (
    id, property_id, subject_kind, subject_id, state, attested_by, because, actor_id, created_at
  )

The search for anything that reads or writes it:
  $ grep -rn "operatingState\|suppressesCare\|blocksOperation\|doNotOperateLine\|currentState\|normaliseState\|DECLARED_STATES\|object_states" \
      server/src server/scripts web/src --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx | grep -v "src/engine/operatingState.ts"
  (no output)

The only INSERT in the repo is in the test:
  server/test/operating-state.test.ts:122  `INSERT INTO object_states (id, property_id, subject_kind, subject_id, state, attested_by, because, actor_id, created_at)`

And there is no route:
  $ grep -n "app\.\(get\|post\|patch\|put\|delete\)(" server/src/index.ts | grep -i "state\|object\|confirm"
  (no output — 45 routes, none of them)
findings.why_it_matters: The module's header presents the mechanism as wired: *"Two consequences follow and both are functions here rather than prose: `suppressesCare` and `blocksOperation`"* (operatingState.ts:33). Neither is reachable. The measured failure the module names — a water heater whose breaker is deliberately off because it is a geothermal preheat store, given a full anode-and-flush care package by the engine, and switched back on by a well-meaning technician — is exactly as available today as before the migration landed, because nothing can record the state and nothing consults it. What makes this worth reporting rather than filing under "not built yet" is the contrast with its neighbours: `engine/confirm.ts:23-33` says plainly *"What is idle here, said plainly — the `adopted` path has no production caller yet"*, and `report/renderGate.ts:70-76` says *"No binder-section renderer exists — Increment 6 is not started"*. `operatingState.ts` makes no such statement, so it reads as live. That is CLAUDE.md §15's own rule — the defect is not that a thing is unbuilt, it is that only some of them say so. The deliberate absence in this migration is the missing `generation_id` column, which is a wall and correct; the table having no caller is not that.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real, a full-text search of `server/src`, `server/scripts` and `web/src` for `object_states` or any `operatingState` export returns nothing outside the module's own file, and running every script in `package.json` against any fixture leaves `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM object_states` at zero. It would be disproved by any importer of `engine/operatingState.js`, or by any API route or script that writes an attestation.

findings.title: `honestyLabels` — the eight-term canonical honesty vocabulary at the top of the binder schema — and the `labelRules.neverUpgraded` flag beside it have no readers; the code carries hardcoded partial copies instead.
findings.evidence:
The declarations:
  schema/binder-schema-v1.json:8-17
    "honestyLabels": [ "observed", "measured", "documented", "reported-by-homeowner",
                       "inferred", "not-inspected", "not-accessible",
                       "specialist-assessment-recommended" ],
  schema/binder-schema-v1.json:19
    "labelRules": { "neverUpgraded": true, "note": "A label can never be upgraded by a later step..." }

The readers:
  $ grep -rn "honestyLabels\|neverUpgraded" server web --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx | wc -l
  0
  (the only hits repo-wide are inside schema/binder-schema-v1.json itself)

The hardcoded copies that took its place:
  server/src/report/clientVoice.ts:61  export type GapLabel = 'not-accessible' | 'not-inspected'
  server/src/report/clientVoice.ts:67-69
    export const POSITIVE_LABELS = [
      'observed', 'measured', 'documented', 'reported-by-homeowner', 'inferred',
    ] as const
  server/src/report/names.ts:265
    const asGapLabel = (value: string): GapLabel =>
      value === 'not-accessible' ? 'not-accessible' : 'not-inspected'

The sibling key in the same object IS read, which is what makes the omission visible:
  server/src/report/names.ts:241  const rules = schema.raw.labelRules
  server/src/report/names.ts:242  ... (rules as Record<string, unknown>).naReasonLabels
findings.why_it_matters: `names.ts:241` reaches into `schema.raw.labelRules` and takes `naReasonLabels` out of it, stepping over `neverUpgraded` on the way — so the schema is being read at exactly the point where this term sits and the term is skipped. The consequence is that the vocabulary has two homes that cannot be reconciled: the schema's list has eight members, `POSITIVE_LABELS` has five, and `asGapLabel` recognises two. `specialist-assessment-recommended` exists in the schema and in no code at all. A term added to or removed from the schema list changes nothing, and the honesty vocabulary is the one thing doctrine 2 says must survive the pipeline unchanged. `clientVoice.ts:53-60` does defend `GapLabel` as a deliberately closed set — *"a label that reaches a client asserts something about their house"* — and that defence is sound for the gap-row type. It does not cover `POSITIVE_LABELS`, and it does not explain why the schema ships a canonical list nothing consults.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real, deleting `honestyLabels` and `neverUpgraded` from `schema/binder-schema-v1.json` breaks no test and changes no output — the schema hash changes and nothing else does. Adding a ninth term to the array likewise reaches no code. It would be disproved by any reader of either key, or by a doctrine scan that cross-checks `POSITIVE_LABELS` against the schema array.

findings.title: The baseline profile's `effortMap` — including `classD_irreduciblyHuman`, which names the reserve figure and the top-items ordering — and its `appliesTo` applicability clause are declared and read by nothing.
findings.evidence:
The declarations:
  schema/profiles/baseline-v1.json:5
    "appliesTo": "visit.kind = baseline",
  schema/profiles/baseline-v1.json:52-57
    "effortMap": {
      "classA_mechanical": ["s1","s2","s3","s5","s12","s17"],
      "classB_rulesGenerated": ["s11","s13","s15","s19.replacement-windows"],
      "classC_aiDraftsHumanSigns": ["s7.components","s8","s10","s14"],
      "classD_irreduciblyHuman": ["s2.top-items ordering","s19.reserve-figure","client conversation and handover"]
    }

The readers:
  $ grep -rn "effortMap\|appliesTo\|classD_irreduciblyHuman" server/src web/src server/scripts --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx
  (no output)

What `loadProfile` actually takes from the file — audit/schema.ts:200-232 — is `required`, `presentWhenPopulated`, `outOfScope`, `notes`, `profileId`, `version`, `schemaVersion`. `appliesTo` is never compared against the `visitKind` that `runAudit` is given (run.ts, `visitKind` parameter), and the profile path is a hardcoded default: `path = join(schemaRoot, 'profiles', 'baseline-v1.json')`.
findings.why_it_matters: `classD_irreduciblyHuman` is the profile's own machine-readable statement of doctrine 9's Never-AI boundary, and `docs/…Property-Flags-and-Session-Plan_Code-Reply_2026-08-07.md:136` describes a render check keyed on exactly this term plus `neverAI` — neither of which any code reads. `appliesTo` is the second half of a pairing whose first half IS checked: `provenanceOf` (audit/schema.ts:305-317) compares `profile.schemaVersion` against `schema.version` and raises a `versionMismatch` that `run.ts:186` pushes into warnings, so schema/profile drift is caught, while profile/visit-kind drift is not. Today the impact is bounded because only one profile file exists, so the wrong pairing cannot happen. That is what makes it easy to miss: the moment a second profile is added, `runAudit(visitKind: 'monthly')` will silently classify slots against the baseline promise and nothing will say so, and the field that would have refused is already sitting in the file being read.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real, `grep -rn "effortMap\|appliesTo" server web --include=*.ts` returns nothing, and calling `runAudit({ visitKind: 'monthly' })` with the baseline profile produces no warning and no refusal despite the file declaring `visit.kind = baseline`. It would be disproved by any code that reads either key, or by a refusal raised when the kinds disagree.

findings.title: Every column of `object_provenance` — including the `honesty_label` that records whether a care interval was adopted rather than confirmed — is written by `confirmObject` and never read back, and `confirmObject` itself has no caller outside its test.
findings.evidence:
The write:
  server/src/engine/confirm.ts:130-137
    const row = db.prepare(
      `INSERT INTO object_provenance (id, decision_id, object_id, stream, act, honesty_label, ref, actor_id, created_at)
       VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
    )
    row.run(randomUUID(), decisionId, args.objectId, 'identification', 'confirmed', ACT_LABEL.confirmed, object.class_id, args.operatorId, at)

Every occurrence of the table in the repo:
  $ grep -rn "object_provenance" . --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx --include=*.sql | grep -v migrations
  server/src/engine/confirm.ts:131      <- the INSERT
  server/test/engine-confirm.test.ts:82,127   <- test INSERTs
  server/test/operators.test.ts:67      <- a string in an actor-coverage table
  (no SELECT anywhere)

And the entry point has no production caller:
  $ grep -rn "confirmObject" server/src server/scripts web/src --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx
  server/src/engine/confirm.ts:97:export function confirmObject(db: Db, args: ConfirmArgs): ConfirmResult {
  (index.ts declares 45 routes; none of them is an object or confirmation route)
findings.why_it_matters: The migration calls the `CHECK ((act = 'confirmed' AND honesty_label = 'Observed') OR (act = 'adopted' AND honesty_label = 'Inferred'))` **"THE CONSTRAINT THAT IS THE POINT"** (018_object_confirmation.sql:96-108), and the module states the payoff: *"when a care interval turns out wrong, and over five years several will, the record already says nobody claimed to have verified it"* (confirm.ts:18-20). That payoff is a read, and there is no read — no query, no screen, no script surfaces which stream on an object was adopted rather than confirmed. `confirm.ts` does defend building the `adopted` path ahead of a producer — *"the guard has to be in place before the temptation"* — and that defence is good and I accept it for the write path. It does not extend to the read: the row exists to be consulted later, and today the honesty distinction it enforces at write time is invisible at every layer above the table. Lower severity than the other honesty finding because the identification stream is a constant (`'confirmed'`/`'Observed'` always), so nothing is currently lost that could not be recomputed — but that stops being true the first time `derived` carries a research interval.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real, a grep for `object_provenance` finds one INSERT in `server/src` and no SELECT anywhere, and `confirmObject` has no importer outside `server/test`. It would be disproved by any query against the table, or by an API route or script that calls `confirmObject`.

finders.note:
Method: I extracted all 589 columns declared across the 26 migration files with a parser, cross-referenced each against every non-migration occurrence in `server/`, `web/`, `schema/` and `prompts/` (snake_case and camelCase), then hand-traced the low-occurrence set to separate writes from reads. Separately I enumerated every JSON key in `schema/binder-schema-v1.json`, `class-frame-v1.json`, `client-names-v1.json`, `owner-question-wording-v1.json`, `retirement-lineage-v1.json`, `profiles/baseline-v1.json`, and every key of the import config snapshot as it actually appears in `fixtures/walk-2026-07-31`, and looked for a reader for each.

Deliberately not reported, because the code argues for them and the argument holds: the absent `source_url` column in 024 (the wall that makes `Documented` unreachable); the absent `generation_id` in 023 (the wall that stops a model proposing an operating state); `componentAliases`, which `audit/binding.ts:168` says must never bind and which `scripts/component-types.ts` does consume; `Slot.defaultLabel`, which `server/test/doctrine.test.ts:2147` states plainly has no reader yet and explains why the type was fixed anyway; `outsideHonestyVocabulary` and `gate()`, which `renderGate.ts:70-76` says are built ahead of Increment 6 on purpose; `inbox_refs.assigned_zone_id`/`assigned_pin_number`, never written and never read; and the prose blocks in the schema (`slotKinds`, `triggerGrammar`, `technologySection`, the `*Rule`/`*Note` keys), which are documentation rather than data.

Two things I could not settle by reading and could not run: the repo has no `node_modules` and `better-sqlite3`/`sharp` are native, so I could not execute the audit to observe the record-set states empirically — finding 1 is derived from an unbranching code path (`sources.ts:124` → `run.ts:229` → `run.ts:470` → `completeness.ts:365` → `completeness.ts:425`) with the profile's own `required` list, and the first thing to do with it is run it. And I did not audit `schema/reference/maintenance-schedule-v1.json` or the `/prompts` config files key by key; the class frame I checked only far enough to establish that `classes[].replacementHorizon`, `careCategories`, `inspectionPoints`, `opportunityConditions` and `ownerQuestions` are consumed solely by `classFrame.ts`'s own validators, and that `auditClassFrame` — the function that runs all five of those validators — is called by tests and by no script or server path.

finders.lens: Values computed and never read — exported functions with no non-test caller, object fields populated on a write path and read on no path, and computed results discarded by the one consumer that wanted them.

findings.title: The pass-3 "unmodelled answer keys" report is re-derived from the stored record instead of read from it, so it prints the builder's own bookkeeping fields as things the model said.
findings.evidence:
`normaliseMatch` computes the value (server/src/ai/tasks/matchComplete.ts:448):

    const MODELLED = new Set(['located', 'couldNotLocate', 'additional', 'unsure'])
    const unmodelledKeys = Object.entries(output as unknown as Record<string, unknown>)
      .filter(([k]) => !MODELLED.has(k))

It is stored: `recordGeneration({ ..., output: stored, ... })` → `JSON.stringify(args.output)` (server/src/ai/queue.ts:398). `grep -rn "unmodelledKeys" server/scripts server/src/index.ts web/src` returns NOTHING — no reader anywhere.

The only place that reports the signal recomputes it over the WRONG object (server/scripts/match.ts:151-166):

    `SELECT output FROM ai_generations WHERE ... task IN ('match_known','enumerate_room')`
    const MODELLED = new Set(['located', 'couldNotLocate', 'additional', 'unsure'])
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(o)) { if (MODELLED.has(k) || seen.has(k)) continue; seen.set(k, ...) }
    console.log(`\n⚑ ${seen.size} answer key(s) this build does not model. NOTHING here became an object:`)

`output` holds a `StoredMatch` (12 top-level keys), not the model's `MatchOutput` (5). Replaying that exact loop over a StoredMatch:

    $ node -e '...same loop over a StoredMatch...'
    ⚑ 8 answer key(s) this build does not model. NOTHING here became an object:
        question: match_known
        evidenceless: []

finders.note:
Method: enumerated all 495 top-level exports in server/src and web/src and checked each for a caller outside its own file and outside server/test; built an import-reachability graph from every real entry point (server/src/index.ts, web/src/main.tsx, all 15 server/scripts/*.ts, the three golden runners, operators/cli.ts) — ten modules are unreachable; and scanned every interface field for a `.field` read anywhere outside its declaring file. Two findings were demonstrated by execution rather than reading: the `unconfirmed_objects` false positive was reproduced by calling `scoreRun` against the committed room record with tsx, and the `unmodelledKeys` mis-report was reproduced by replaying scripts/match.ts's exact loop over a StoredMatch-shaped JSON in node.

Deliberate-by-comment cases I checked and am NOT reporting: `report/renderGate.ts` (header argues at length that the gate must exist before Increment 6's renderer), `engine/confirm.ts`'s `adopted` half (explicitly declared idle — I report only that the `confirmed` half is equally callerless while the header implies otherwise), `audit/facts.ts:57 VisitFacts.disagreements` (documented as empty until an intake form exists), `ai/golden-routing.ts` (header states no fixture set can exist yet and why), `audit/sources.ts` READERS with no `count` (deliberately unread, named), and `object_states` / `engine/operatingState.ts` — the Frame-Bracket note of 2026-08-11 declares it unbuilt by intent, though its wording ("a table with a reader and no writer") is wrong in one direction: there is no reader either; nothing queries `object_states` and `doNotOperateLine`/`suppressesCare`/`blocksOperation` have no production caller.

Ruled out on inspection: `import/integrity.ts RefCheck.dangling`, `overlay/fields.ts FORBIDDEN_FIELDS`/`CORRECTABLE_FIELDS`, `report/render.ts Brand.lockup`, `audit/run.ts statusDisagreements` (reaches the operator via `warnings`), `import/report.ts` findings and bytes-by-kind (both rendered), `ai/queue.ts wouldExceedCap` (redundant wrapper; the cap is enforced at worker.ts:123), and `Edition.withheld` (rendered in GapReport.tsx).

Could not reach: `node_modules` is absent, so `npm test` and `tsc` could not be run — I could not confirm the 1224-green claim myself, and probes needing `better-sqlite3` (a live match generation end-to-end) had to be simulated from the exact source of the loop instead. `engine/assembly.ts` + `engine/plan.ts` + `engine/runRecord.ts` are a fourth unreachable cluster, apparently superseded by `engine/identify.ts` (Increment 5 §3); I could not establish from the code whether that supersession was intended, so I left it out rather than guess.

The claim in the migration:

findings.why_it_matters: "The lane and its evidence arrive together or not at all" is stated as a property of the system and is enforced by nothing: the write itself expresses the forbidden state with `?? null`, and no code path — not the score harness, not the proposals fixture, not the comparison report, not `npm run passes` — can distinguish a `plate` object with evidence behind it from one without. Today `resolutionOf` is built from the same `resolved = 1` set that seeds the room inventory, so the NULL branch is probably not taken — but there is no assertion, no report line and no reader that would notice the day it is, and `plate` is the lane whose whole selling point is that it is close to deterministic.

    server/src/ai/accept.ts:388   confidence: g.confidence,            (in `toProposal`)

The writer, with the field optional:

Every call site — worker.ts:199, nameplate.ts:166, nameplate.ts:243, identify.ts:629, matchComplete.ts:690, pinType.ts:298, readSurfaces.ts:501, routing.ts:364, resolveProduct.ts:405 — and none of them names it:

finders.note:
Covered: all 26 files in server/src/db/migrations read in order, with attention to every DROP/RENAME/rebuild (002 pins, 003 verifications+field_fixes, 010 imports/audit_runs/zones/pins/media/resolutions, 011 the two partial unique indexes, 015 visit_date→planned_date, 019 objects); git history for deleted files (none under server/src or web/src — every refactor is in place) and `git log -S` on the identifiers each migration touches.

Verified mechanically rather than by reading: (1) built the live schema by running all migrations into an in-memory database and cross-checked every one of 484 columns against the source tree; (2) parsed every INSERT/UPDATE in server/src, server/scripts and web/src to find columns with no writer — only `object_states` and the deliberate `inbox_refs` assignment columns came back; (3) scanned every SQL-shaped line for identifiers absent from the schema, to catch a reader pointing at a dropped column — none found, so no literal dangling column reader survives any of the rebuilds; (4) checked foreign keys and `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` after all migrations (clean, cascades intact on the objects children despite 019's rebuild); (5) cross-checked every `/api/...` path the web calls against the express routes (all present; the reverse direction has four server-only routes — item-series, desk-work, house-style/rules, operators — which the code argues are deliberately API-only); (6) reproduced finding 1 end to end by importing both committed fixtures and printing the three planners' outputs side by side.

Two things I could not reach. The AI passes were exercised as plans only — no API key, so no model call ran and I could not observe what a real pass-3 answer does to `resolution_id` in practice; the NULL branch at matchComplete.ts:573 is argued from the code rather than seen. And `npm test` was not run (deps were absent; I installed them for the schema work but did not re-run the suite), so I am reporting on what the tests do not cover rather than confirming the 1224 pass here.

Migration 019 is worth a second pair of eyes for a reason I could not turn into a finding: it does `PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF` … `DROP TABLE objects` … `RENAME` without the `-- no-transaction` marker, so the pragma is the silent no-op that 010's own header and `server/src/db/index.ts:46-61` warn about. It happens to be harmless — `objects` and its three child tables were empty when it ran, and `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` comes back clean — but the protection the file believes it has is not in effect, and the next rebuild of a populated table copied from this template would not be so lucky.

Covered: every table created in server/src/db/migrations/001–026 (48 CREATE TABLEs, 44 live after rebuilds), mapped writer→reader by grepping all INSERT/UPDATE and all `FROM <table>`/`JOIN <table>` in server/src, server/scripts and web/src, then column-by-column (snake_case and camelCase) for columns referenced ≤2 times. THE LANE SWEEP HELD. Run against the reference import (probe, since deleted):
  before  totals : rows 20 in columns 20 withheld 0

  after   column : missing-from-them  because: moved here by hand  included: true

findings.why_it_matters: The gap report is the one-page artifact a homeowner receives, and a signed edition is a dated snapshot the binder stands on. A row that a concierge deliberately moved leaves the document with no trace: `withheld` — the mechanism built precisely so "a withheld row nobody hears about is a dropped row with extra steps" cannot happen — stays empty, the `render.nothing-included` guard still sees 20 included rows, the House Style lint never sees the sentence, and neither the desk screen (GapReport.tsx:148 re-filters `draft.rows` by column the same way) nor the edition record reports 19 of 20. findings.falsifiable_as: If real: POST /api/properties/:id/report/rows/:rowKey/column with body {"column":"missing-from-them"} returns 201; the subsequent GET of the draft shows that row still in `rows` with `included: true` and `columnBecause: "moved here by hand"`, present in none of `columns[].rows`, and absent from `withheld`; signing produces an edition whose HTML omits the sentence and whose `withheld` array is empty. findings.title: `reportUnmodelled()` reads the repo's own stored shape instead of the model's answer, so it prints eight of this build's own field names as "answer keys this build does not model" on every run, and can never print a real one.
findings.evidence:
match.ts:152  `SELECT output FROM ai_generations WHERE visit_id = ? AND task IN ('match_known','enumerate_room') ...`
match.ts:157  `const MODELLED = new Set(['located', 'couldNotLocate', 'additional', 'unsure'])`
match.ts:168  ``console.log(`\n⚑ ${seen.size} answer key(s) this build does not model. NOTHING here became an object:`)``

But `ai_generations.output` is not the model's answer. queue.ts:398 stores `JSON.stringify(args.output ?? null)`, and matchComplete.ts:683 passes `output: stored` — the `StoredMatch`, whose own keys are question, located, evidenceless, unmodelledKeys, couldNotLocate, additional, unsure, roomNote, unknownProducts, unknownClasses, strayEvidence, danglingParents. The raw `output` from `runVisionTask` is normalised at matchComplete.ts:683 and then discarded; it is written nowhere.

Replaying the function body verbatim over one schema-valid answer (probe, since deleted):
  ⚑ 8 answer key(s) this build does not model. NOTHING here became an object:
      question: match_known
      evidenceless: []
      unmodelledKeys: [{"key":"roomNote","preview":"two frames are of the same wall"}]
      roomNote: two frames are of the same wall
      unknownProducts: []
      unknownClasses: []
      strayEvidence: []
      danglingParents: []

The query also has no `human_decision` or failure filter, so worker.ts:213's failure rows — `output: { failed: true, code: e.code, message: e.message }` — add `failed`, `code` and `message` to the same list.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the printer the 2026-08-13 "stop discarding" ruling produced, and its own doc-comment states the standard it fails: *"a bucket that is reported into a variable nobody prints is the same drop one layer up, so it is printed here."* What it prints is eight of the repo's own storage field names, every run, forever — including `unmodelledKeys` itself rendered as an opaque 160-character JSON blob rather than unpacked. An operator reading `⚑ 8 answer key(s) this build does not model` after every pass-3 run learns within two runs to ignore the banner, which is the exact degradation the Verification-Discipline note calls out ("a check that cries wolf degrades the one thing it exists to provide"). And because the raw answer is never persisted, the drop the ruling was made to stop is still total — the only surviving record of what the model actually said outside the four modelled arrays is `stored.unmodelledKeys`, and this function does not read it.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real: `npm run match -- --visit <id> --run --owner-property` against any visit that has pass-3 generations prints the ⚑ banner naming `question`, `roomNote`, `strayEvidence`, `danglingParents`, `unknownProducts`, `unknownClasses`, `evidenceless` and `unmodelledKeys` — none of which is a model answer key. If it were reading the model's answer, it would print nothing (MATCH_SCHEMA is `additionalProperties: false`, so no extra key can arrive) and `seen.size === 0` would return early at match.ts:167. I reproduced the eight-key output by replaying the function body over `JSON.stringify(normaliseMatch(...))`. Grep confirms no test imports this script.

findings.title: `normaliseMatch`'s MODELLED set omits `roomNote`, which MATCH_SCHEMA makes required — so the un-modelled-key channel fires falsely on every real call and, because the schema forbids extra properties, can never fire truly.
findings.evidence:
matchComplete.ts:88   `required: ['located', 'couldNotLocate', 'additional', 'unsure', 'roomNote'],`  (with `additionalProperties: false` at :87)
matchComplete.ts:448  `const MODELLED = new Set(['located', 'couldNotLocate', 'additional', 'unsure'])`
matchComplete.ts:531  `roomNote: typeof output.roomNote === 'string' ? output.roomNote : '',`   — it *is* modelled, and stored

Probe on one schema-valid answer (since deleted):
  schema required : [ 'located', 'couldNotLocate', 'additional', 'unsure', 'roomNote' ]
  additionalProps : false
  unmodelledKeys  : [{"key":"roomNote","preview":"the utility room is tight; two frames are of the same wall"}]
  roomNote stored : "the utility room is tight; two frames are of the same wall"

The negative test that is supposed to make the check falsifiable uses an input the API cannot return — match-complete.test.ts:429 asserts `unmodelledKeys` is `[]` for `{ located: [], couldNotLocate: [], additional: [], unsure: [] }`, an object missing the required `roomNote`. Its comment reads: "The half that lets the check fail: a reporter that always fires is noise." It always fires.
findings.why_it_matters: `StoredMatch.unmodelledKeys` is documented as "where a hypothesis lands first" and as the specification for an unbuilt channel — so the content of this bucket is meant to be read as evidence about what the model wanted to say. It contains one entry, `roomNote`, on every call, and cannot contain anything else: the output schema is strict, so the set of possible top-level keys is exactly the five in `required`. The bucket therefore carries no information at all, while the field it names is simultaneously stored and used. Nothing links MODELLED to `MatchOutput`'s keys, so typecheck cannot notice, and the two copies of the list (here and match.ts:157) can drift independently.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real: calling `normaliseMatch` with any object carrying all five schema-required keys returns `unmodelledKeys` containing `roomNote` while `stored.roomNote` holds the same string. If it were not real, `roomNote` would be in MODELLED and the bucket would be empty for a schema-valid answer. I ran it; output quoted above. The disproof would be an answer shape the API can return that carries a sixth top-level key — `additionalProperties: false` at matchComplete.ts:87 rules that out.

findings.title: `declarationOf` returns the same `{ tier: 'standard', text: null }` for four different states, one of which is "the config never declared this item" — and the caller stamps `certain: true, unrecognised: []` beside it.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the v4 path — "v4 ships the field's own resolved set and this module reads it" (activeItems.ts:15) — i.e. the production path, and the failure it exists to prevent is named in the same header: "two apps disagreeing about whether an item was ever due, with nothing to error." An item id the field ships that this import's config does not declare is exactly that divergence, and it arrives as an ordinary standard-tier item whose record positively claims `certain: true` and `unrecognised: []`, with no warning on the set and no line on the import report. Doctrine 7 requires unknown item ids to be preserved, displayed, counted and marked unrecognised; three of the four are missing. It is also the third state the Verification-Discipline note's rule 6 asks for — declared-standard vs never-declared — collapsed into the reassuring one.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real: insert one `active_items` row with `origin='received'` whose `item_id` is absent from the import's `config_snapshots.snapshot`, then call `activeItemSet(db, propertyId)` — the item comes back with `tier: 'standard'`, `itemText: null`, `certain: true`, `unrecognised: []`, and `set.warnings` is empty. If it were not real, either the fall-through at activeItems.ts:307 would return a distinguishable state, or `unrecognised` would name the id, or `checkVocabulary` would have flagged it at import. I ran exactly this; output quoted above. Reachability caveat, stated rather than glossed: both fixtures are v3 and adapters/v3.ts:294 hardcodes `activeItems: []`, so `fromReceived` is idle today — the defect is on the path that becomes live with the v4 adapter, and no fixture can currently exercise it.

findings.title: Twelve anomaly buckets across the four AI task normalisers are computed, documented as "reported, never dropped", and read by nothing outside the module that writes them.
findings.evidence:
readSurfaces.ts:364-368:
```
    // A photograph the model neither read nor declared empty. **Not the same as
    // "no text" and it must not be counted as one** — nobody said anything about
    // it, which is a hole rather than a result.
    unaccounted: [...sent].filter((m) => !mentioned.has(m)),
```
The module header at readSurfaces.ts:310-316 says: "Turn one answer into something storable. **Nothing is discarded.** ... each is kept and reported. Doctrine 6."

Reader count outside `server/src/ai/tasks/` (grep over server/src, web/src, server/scripts for each name; the two `unaccounted` hits are prose in engine/score.ts comments, and every `unanswered` hit is an unrelated identifier in audit/ and plan/):
  strayEvidence 0 · unknownClasses 0 · unevidenced 0 · unknownSurfaces 0 · strayLabels 0
  unaccounted 0 · demoted 0 · strayAnswers 0 · evidenceless 0 · danglingParents 0
  unknownProducts 0 · unmodelledKeys 0

Other instances with the same doc-comment/no-reader pattern:
  identify.ts:520      `unevidenced,`        header at :464 — "**Nothing is discarded.** ... each is kept, corrected where correction is honest, and reported. Doctrine 6"
  resolveProduct.ts:304 `demoted,`           header at :259 — "**Nothing is discarded.**"
  matchComplete.ts:521-524  `evidenceless`, `strayEvidence`, `danglingParents`, `unknownProducts`, `unknownClasses`

All thirteen live only inside the `ai_generations.output` JSON blob (queue.ts:398). No script prints them (`grep -n "stray|dangling|evidenceless|unknownProduct|unknownClass" server/scripts/*.ts` → nothing), no API route returns them, and `buildAssists` (ai/screen.ts:163) handles only EXTRACT_TASK and PIN_TYPE_TASK, so pass-1/2/3 proposals never reach a screen.
findings.why_it_matters: The repo states the applicable standard itself, in match.ts:141: *"a bucket that is reported into a variable nobody prints is the same drop one layer up."* That standard was applied to exactly one of thirteen buckets, and the one printer it produced reads the wrong object (see the `reportUnmodelled` finding). The sharpest instance is `unaccounted`: a photograph pass 1 sent to the model and got no answer about at all — neither a label nor a `noText` declaration. Its own comment says it "must not be counted as" no-text, because that is a hole rather than a result. Today the distinction is drawn correctly in memory and then dissolved: downstream, both look identical, because nothing reads the field. `evidenceless` has a documented, paid-for instance behind it ("Pressurized bladder tank isolation hardware ... became the run's only false positive") — the object is refused, and the refusal is announced to nobody.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real: `grep -rn --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx '<bucket-name>' server/src web/src server/scripts | grep -v '^server/src/ai/tasks/'` returns zero substantive hits for all twelve names, and reading a `match_known` / `read_surfaces` / `resolve_product` / `identify_objects` run's output requires hand-querying `ai_generations.output` in SQLite. If it were not real, at least one runner script, API route or web page would name the field. I ran the grep; counts quoted above. This is not a coverage complaint — the values are correctly computed and correctly named; the claim is only that no path carries them to a reader.

finders.note:
Covered: the whole import path (adapters/v3, canonical, vocabulary, integrity, persist, media, report), all four AI task normalisers plus routing/nameplate/pinType, ai/client, ai/queue, ai/worker, ai/accept, ai/screen, the audit modules (activeItems, carriedItems, zoneAudit, completeness, binding), the engine (identify, assembly, compare, lanes, classFrame, confirm), plan/sessionPlan, the whole report path (draft, clientVoice, names, render, renderGate, houseStyle), desk/work, the Express routes in index.ts, and the web pages. I read every `catch` block in server/src, every bare `continue`, and all 96 `?? []` / `?? {}` sites.

Checked and cleared — things that look like the target and are not: `extractZip`'s `skipped` list is surfaced as a `media.unsafe-archive-entry` check in runImport.ts:137; `checkVocabulary` is thorough on resolutions, pins, zones, media, notes, chats and events, counts everything and names its denominators; `resolveToZones` and `assembleZone` report `unresolved` / `unconsumed` / `unavailable` into the plan note; `carriedItems` warns by name on an undeclared na reason; `withheld()` in clientVoice mirrors `clientRow()`'s two null branches exactly; `blockedSlots` mirrors `gate()`'s two refusals; media rows with a null id crash on a NOT NULL column rather than being dropped. The unrecognised-`kind` coercion in `normaliseResolve` (resolveProduct.ts:273) and the frame-shape guard in `framesOf` (names.ts:56) are both real cannot-fail defaults, but the first is unreachable behind an enum in the output schema and the second currently drops nothing (all 3 declared `byReason` frames load) — I left both out rather than pad the list.

Two things I could not reach: the `active_items` received path has no fixture (both exports are v3 and adapters/v3.ts:294 hardcodes an empty array), so I exercised it by inserting a row directly; and I could not run any real model call, so the `unmodelledKeys` findings rest on `MATCH_SCHEMA`'s `additionalProperties: false` plus a replay of the exact code over a schema-valid object rather than on a live API response.

Probe files were written under server/tmp-probe/ and deleted; `git status` is clean apart from a pre-existing untracked `server/test/_scratch_seed.ts` that I did not create or touch.

finders.lens: checks whose output does not depend on what they check

findings.title: The personal-data scan never reads `modelRead`, the field that carries most of the plate text it exists to look at.
findings.evidence:
`scanForPersonalData` builds its field list from exactly two sources:

```ts
// proposalFixture.ts:231-234
const fields: { where: PersonalDataHit['where']; text: string }[] = [
  { where: 'label', text: p.label },
  ...p.models.map((m) => ({ where: 'model' as const, text: m })),
]
```

But `buildFixture` writes a third text field into every fixture (proposalFixture.ts:115):

```ts
...(p.modelRead ? { modelRead: p.modelRead } : {}),
```

and `PersonalDataHit.where` is typed `'label' | 'model'` (line 189), so there is structurally no value a hit could carry to name it.

Planted the thing the scan forbids and it did not fire:

```
$ node --import tsx test/_scratch_t1.ts
fixture proposal: {"id":"o1",...,"models":[],"modelRead":"Gas fitter licence 12345 613-555-0142 at 1 Nowhere Road"}
scan hits: []
```

That string contains all three of the shapes the scan claims to catch (licence-by-word, phone, address) and produced zero hits, because it is in the unread field.

The committed public fixture already carries the field, and carries it more often than the one that IS scanned:

```
$ node -e "...fixtures/proposals/mechanical-room_pass3-rerun_2026-08-13.json..."
proposals: 50  carrying modelRead: 15
sample modelRead values: [ '45MHP1B1STAA', 'WOB5 PC1', '600545B', 'G9-60SDE-30 260', 'DMF150', 'UT-450 CE', ... ]
carrying models[]: 7
```

The test that claims whole-run coverage cannot see it either — `proposal-fixture.test.ts:190` ("is clean on the whole of a real run") builds its proposals through `fromDb`, which hardcodes `models: []` (line 80) and never sets `modelRead`, so that assertion exercises label text only.
findings.why_it_matters: `npm run proposals` prints "The personal-data scan found nothing" and tells the operator "Read the labels before this file goes anywhere public" (scripts/proposals.ts:235-242). This repository is public, and CLAUDE.md §14 names precisely this channel: "Identification reads plates, and a label can come back carrying an address or a licence number." `modelRead` IS the plate reading — pass 3's own transcription of the label — and it is the half of the fixture the scan is blind to. A reviewer following the printed instruction reads the labels and never learns there is a second text column. `models[]` is documented at line 64 as the deprecated one ("no longer what rule 6 reads"); the scan reads the deprecated field and skips the current one.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real, adding `{ where: 'modelRead', text: p.modelRead }` to the `fields` array makes the planted string above produce three hits instead of zero, and re-running the scan over `fixtures/proposals/mechanical-room_pass3-rerun_2026-08-13.json` now examines 15 additional strings that were previously unexamined. It would be disproved if `modelRead` could never reach a fixture (it does — 15 of 50 in the committed one) or if some other guard scanned it before publication (grep for `scanForPersonalData` returns two call sites: scripts/proposals.ts:232 and the test; neither reads `modelRead`).

findings.title: The binder draft's Findings count is `WHERE 1 = 0` — hardwired to zero — and the draft then prints that the visit failed to supply findings.
findings.evidence:
```ts
// binder.ts:122-125 — the counts map, three real queries and one tautology
['s7.components', one(`SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM objects WHERE import_id = ? AND derived_from IS NOT NULL`, importId)],
['s4.profile',    one('SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM zones WHERE import_id = ?', importId)],
['s12.alarms',    one(`... class_id LIKE '%alarm%'`, importId)],
['s10.findings',  one('SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM audit_slots WHERE 1 = 0')],
```

`WHERE 1 = 0` occurs exactly once in the whole repo, carries no comment, and takes no `importId` parameter. `s10.findings` is `required` in `schema/profiles/baseline-v1.json`, so `buildDraft` falls to the last branch (binderDraft.ts:172-182) and — because the slot is not in `NO_PRODUCER` and `awaiting` is never passed — emits `emptyReason: 'not-captured'`:

```ts
// binderDraft.ts:182
: '**GAP — this ought to be here and is not.** The producer exists and the visit did not supply it.'
```

Ran the real command against a seeded database:

```
$ node --import tsx scripts/binder.ts --visit <v>
**Findings** ⚑

**GAP — this ought to be here and is not.** The producer exists and the visit did not supply it.

**Concerns — the tracked subset** ⚑

**GAP — nothing in the builder can fill this yet.** No pass, screen or import produces it.
```

A producer does exist and is already read elsewhere — `import/report.ts:186` counts `resolutions WHERE records_finding = 1` and the import-report screen shows the failed-check / confirmed-absence breakdown off it. On the walk fixture:

```
walk fixture findings (resolutions.records_finding=1): 2
what binder.ts counts for s10.findings:                0
```

The script's own guard cannot see this: `badCounts` (binder.ts:131) checks that every KEY is a declared slot id and says nothing about whether the query reads anything. `binder-draft.test.ts` tests `buildDraft` with hand-built count maps; the one process-level assertion (score-script.test.ts:211) checks only `s7.components`.
findings.why_it_matters: This draft's entire stated purpose is that an outside reviewer can tell a missing producer from a missing fact — "a binder showing thirteen legitimately-empty sections as thirteen holes gets reviewed on the wrong thirteen things, and the reviewer's attention is what this document is spending" (binder.ts:19-21). Findings is the one slot where the draft asserts the opposite of the truth: it says the producer exists and the house supplied nothing, when the house supplied two findings and the query supplied nothing. `s10.concerns` on the very next line gets this right, which is what makes the wrong sentence read as considered. And CLAUDE.md §5 calls collapsing findings the most damaging modelling mistake available here.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real, replacing the query with `SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM resolutions WHERE import_id = ? AND records_finding = 1` (passing `importId`) makes the walk-fixture draft render "2 entries" for Findings instead of a gap, and no other output changes. It would be disproved if `audit_slots` had no rows under any circumstance (it is written by `audit/run.ts:356`) or if a comment somewhere argued the zero was deliberate — there is none, and the honest form of a deliberate zero in this script is an entry in `NO_PRODUCER`, which `s10.concerns` has and `s10.findings` does not.

findings.title: `read.ts` and `match.ts` report stored state through a `report()` that takes no run outcome, so it cannot distinguish "this run found these" from "this run did nothing" — the exact bug fixed in their sibling `resolve.ts` and nowhere else.
findings.why_it_matters: Pass 1 and pass 3 are the two passes that cost money and send photographs of the inside of a house. A run whose calls all fail (401, spend cap, transport) still ends with `Ran 0, failed 16` followed by a confident table of labels or objects from an earlier run — the same presentation that already misled a runner session on 2026-08-13 in pass 2. `read.ts`'s and `match.ts`'s plan-only paths are worse than pass 2's: they print the table after a command that by definition ran nothing, with no qualifier at all. Verification-discipline rule 5 and rule 13 both say the fix for this class is applied to the class; here it was applied to the one file the incident happened in.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real, giving `read.ts` and `match.ts` the same `report(ran, failed)` signature changes their output on exactly two inputs — the plan-only path and a drain where `result.ran === 0` — and changes nothing else. It would be disproved if either script already carried a distinguishing signal (grep for `NOTHING RAN` returns only resolve.ts:176) or if a comment argued the omission was deliberate (read.ts's only comment on `report` is about function hoisting at line 82-84; match.ts has none).

findings.title: `SCANNED_ROOTS` excludes `server/scripts`, so doctrine scans that claim "anywhere in the codebase" and "at all" cannot see 2,700 lines of database-touching code — and three files there break one of them.
findings.evidence:
```ts
// doctrine.test.ts:136-140
/** The roots any scan walks. Kept here so the audit below can walk them all. */
const SCANNED_ROOTS = [
  join(repoRoot, 'server', 'src'),
  join(repoRoot, 'web', 'src'),
]
```

The comment is not true: one scan does walk `server/scripts` (line 3015, the `HOUSESTEADY_OPERATOR` check), which is why the directory is known to be scannable. Every other scan is scoped to `serverSrc`, including ones whose titles claim repo-wide reach — line 160 `'never UPDATEs or DELETEs a captured row, anywhere in the codebase'`, and:

```ts
// doctrine.test.ts:586-596
it('lets only the acceptance path read ai_generations at all', () => {
  const ALLOWED = [join('ai','accept.ts'), join('ai','queue.ts'), join('overlay','store.ts')]
  const offenders = sourceFiles(serverSrc)
    .filter((f) => /\bai_generations\b/.test(codeOf(f)))
    .filter((f) => !ALLOWED.some((a) => f.endsWith(a)))
  assert.deepEqual(offenders, [], 'a read path touching ai_generations is how an unsigned value reaches the screen')
})
```

Re-running that exact predicate with `server/scripts` added to the walk:

```
offenders if the walk included server/scripts:
  server/scripts/match.ts       // SELECT output FROM ai_generations ... and prints the raw output
  server/scripts/proposals.ts   // SELECT id, task, created_at FROM ai_generations
  server/scripts/smoke.ts       // SELECT model, input_tokens, ... FROM ai_generations
```

I applied the other two source-shape scans to the same extended walk to size the gap honestly — the actor-column scan and the inline-prompt scan both come back empty, and `make-fixture.ts`'s `'claude-sonnet-5'` literals are fixture data rather than a model call. So the concrete count today is three, all against the one scan that says "at all". `SCANNED_ROOTS` also feeds the extension audit at line 2825, so `server/scripts` is outside that too: a `.tsx` or a new extension appearing there would not be declared or refused.
findings.why_it_matters: These scans are this repo's stated mechanism for doctrine that no behavioural test can reach — "the way this doctrine breaks is not by someone deciding to render proposals, it is by a read path quietly joining ai_generations for convenience." Two of the three reads have arguments beside them (match.ts:138-148 argues for printing unmodelled keys; smoke.ts reads the cost ledger), but none of them is an exemption anybody made: they are outside the scan's reach, so the green result is not evidence for the sentence the test's name asserts. The `NOT_SCANNED` map at line 57 shows the repo's own convention — an exclusion is a declared decision with a reason — and no such declaration exists for this root.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real, adding `join(repoRoot,'server','scripts')` to `SCANNED_ROOTS` and to the `ai_generations` scan's walk turns that test red naming match.ts, proposals.ts and smoke.ts, forcing three explicit ALLOWED entries or three changes; the actor-column and model-id scans stay green. It would be disproved by a comment anywhere declaring server/scripts out of scope for doctrine scans — I grepped doctrine.test.ts for "scripts" and the only three hits are the operator scan and its prose.

finders.note:
Read CLAUDE.md and `docs/HouseSteady_Binder-Builder_Note_Verification-Discipline_2026-07-28.md` (rules 1-16) first, then worked the lens by execution rather than by reading.

**Process-coverage map for `server/scripts/` (the lens asked for this explicitly).** Only three scripts are ever spawned by a test: `score.ts` (score-script.test.ts, five cases), `binder.ts` (score-script.test.ts:207, one assertion, on `s7.components` only), `compare.ts` (object-lanes.test.ts:322, three cases). The other twelve — `identify.ts`, `import-export.ts`, `make-fixture.ts`, `match.ts`, `passes.ts`, `plan-fixture.ts`, `preflight.ts`, `proposals.ts`, `read.ts`, `resolve.ts`, `smoke.ts`, `component-types.ts` — have no test that runs them as a process. Three of them (`proposals`, `passes`, `import-export`) are named in CLAUDE.md §16 as "the commands". Two of my four findings live in that unrun set. Separately and outside the lens: `npm run import-export` is documented in §16 but is not a script in either `package.json`; the header's `npx tsx server/scripts/import-export.ts` is the working form.

**I ran the untested scripts.** Seeded a scratch database from `fixtures/walk-2026-07-31/` and executed `read.ts`, `resolve.ts`, `match.ts`, `passes.ts`, `proposals.ts` and `binder.ts` as processes. All six print and exit 0 — none repeats the 2026-08-13 silent-exit bug. The defects I found in them are in what they print, not whether they print.

**Checked and cleared, so nobody repeats the work.** (a) Every two-marker `.slice(indexOf, indexOf)` in the test suite — nine in doctrine.test.ts, plus engine-identify, gap-report and placement-and-memory — locates both boundaries in the current sources; I verified each numerically. findings.title: The binder draft counts findings with a query that can never return a row, then tells the reader the visit did not supply them.
findings.evidence:
server/scripts/binder.ts:125 —
  ['s10.findings', one(`SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM audit_slots WHERE 1 = 0`)],

The other three entries in the same `counts` map are real queries against real tables. This one has no comment defending it, and `WHERE 1 = 0` returns 0 for every visit that has ever existed.

The producer it should be reading does exist. server/src/import/report.ts:185 —
  `SELECT item_id, kind, result, reason_id, scope_kind FROM resolutions
     WHERE import_id = ? AND records_finding = 1 ORDER BY item_id`
and schema/binder-schema-v1.json declares s10.findings' sources as `field.check:fail` and `field.na:recordsFinding` — exactly those rows.

Measured by importing both committed fixtures into a fresh in-memory db and running binder.ts's own count expressions (probe via `npx tsx`, since deleted):
  reference: resolutions with records_finding=1 → 4   binder.ts's s10.findings query → 0
  walk:      resolutions with records_finding=1 → 2   binder.ts's s10.findings query → 0

The rendered markdown for the walk import, verbatim:
  ### 10. Baseline condition assessment
  **Findings** ⚑
  **GAP — this ought to be here and is not.** The producer exists and the visit did not supply it.
findings.why_it_matters: Findings is the one stream CLAUDE.md §5 singles out — `result: fail` plus `na` where `recordsFinding` is true, the failed checks and the confirmed absences that feed the condition assessment. The only rendering of the binder this repo has says the visit supplied none, on both fixtures, while the database holds four and two. It is not a blank the reader can chase; it is a sentence that assigns the absence to the house.
findings.falsifiable_as: If this were real, `npm run binder -- --visit <id>` on any import carrying a `records_finding = 1` resolution prints "Findings ⚑ / GAP — ... the visit did not supply it" while `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM resolutions WHERE import_id = ? AND records_finding = 1` returns non-zero. It would be disproved if s10.findings were listed in NO_PRODUCER (then the sentence would correctly read "nothing in the builder can fill this yet"), or if `audit_slots` were in fact the store for findings — it is not; server/src/audit/carriedItems.ts:4 says explicitly that the field-checklist stream "is not `audit_slots` and must never be read off it", and doctrine.test.ts:1530 pins that.

findings.title: Sixteen slots the binder draft can never fill are rendered as "The producer exists and the visit did not supply it", which blames the visit for missing software.
findings.evidence:
server/src/report/binderDraft.ts:172-182 —
  emptyReason = data.noProducer.has(slot.id)
    ? 'no-producer'
    : data.awaiting?.has(slot.id)
      ? 'no-data-yet'
      : 'not-captured'
  ...
      : '**GAP — this ought to be here and is not.** The producer exists and the visit did not supply it.'

The caller supplies `noProducer` from a hand-kept list and never supplies `awaiting` at all — server/scripts/binder.ts:137-140:
  const draft = buildDraft(schema, profile, {
    counts,
    noProducer: new Set(Object.keys(NO_PRODUCER)),
  })

And `counts` (binder.ts:105-126) has exactly four keys: s7.components, s4.profile, s12.alarms, s10.findings. Every other slot is structurally zero no matter what the visit contained, so `not-captured` is the default branch for everything the hand-kept list forgot.

Run on both committed fixtures, 19 of the 27 gaps take that branch; 16 of them have no count entry at all:
  s1.shutoff-map · s1.response-procedures · s1.emergency-contacts · s2.property-summary ·
  s2.top-items · s2.tests-in-flight · s2.services-due · s2.missing-records · s2.next-review ·
  s6.profile · s11.warranties · s12.egress · s12.other · s15.custom-schedule ·
  s15.owner-pro-split · s15.both-realities

No producer exists for them. `for s in s1.shutoff-map s1.emergency-contacts s2.top-items s6.profile s11.warranties s12.egress; do grep -rl "$s" --include=*.ts server/src server/scripts; done` returns nothing for any of them. (`s2.next-review` matches only server/src/report/renderGate.ts, which is a gate that refuses it, not a producer.)

binder.ts:76-86 checks the list in one direction only — every id in NO_PRODUCER must be a real slot id. Nothing checks the converse, which is the direction that produces this sentence.
findings.why_it_matters: This document exists to be critiqued by an outside reviewer, and binderDraft.ts:29-34 states the whole reason the reasons are carried: "*Nothing here because no lab result has returned* is a different fact from *nothing here because nobody has built the producer*, and **an outside reviewer can only critique the second**." Sixteen of the twenty-seven gaps are sorted into the half the reviewer cannot act on, and binder.ts:183-186 then prints "⚑ 8 of the 27 gaps are missing PRODUCERS rather than missing data — ... they are what an outside review is for", steering attention away from them by name. The document also carries a claim about the software that is false, in a file whose own comment (binder.ts:118) calls this "a heading in a client-facing draft".
findings.falsifiable_as: If this were real, `npm run binder` on any visit prints "The producer exists and the visit did not supply it" under headings like `s1.shutoff-map` and `s11.warranties`, while a grep for those slot ids across `server/src` and `server/scripts` finds no code that could ever write them. It would be disproved by finding a producer for any of the sixteen, or by binder.ts passing a count key for them — neither exists. Note the three-state design in binderDraft.ts is correct; the defect is that the caller can only ever populate one of the three sets.

server/src/report/houseStyle.ts:109-116 —

    pattern: /\bcondition\s*[::]\s*(poor|fair|good|excellent)\b/i,
    because:

Same run, other constructions House Style names by name:

  PASSES "The panel is a fire hazard."       (pattern has `hazardous`, not `hazard`)

The lint runs in the render path precisely so it sees "the sentence a concierge types into the editor at four o'clock on a Friday" (houseStyle.ts:8-9), and that sentence is written in English, not in enum syntax. The rule catches the machine spelling of the grade and misses the human one, so the only form that can actually occur is the form that ships.

The only guard above it refuses when the *whole* report is empty, never when a column is (render.ts:157-165):

Signing both committed fixtures end to end (import → runAudit → buildDraft → signEdition, probe via npx tsx, since deleted) and extracting the headings:

  walk:      columns in HTML h2: [ 'Missing from us' ]

Deleting the heading does not fix that reading — it removes the client's last cue that there was a column at all, so a document with nothing outstanding and a document where nobody typed anything are byte-identical. findings.title: The property label reaches the client document's title unlinted, because the lint reads `address ?? label` and the title always reads `label`.
findings.evidence: The lint (render.ts:205-206): violations.push(...lint(args.signedByName, 'the signature line')) violations.push(...lint(args.property.address ?? args.property.label, 'the address in the header')) The render (render.ts:337 and 369): Gap report — ${esc(args.property.label)} ...Gap report${esc(args.property.address ?? args.property.label)}... So whenever `address` is non-null — the normal case, and what the repo's own test fixtures use — `label` is composed into the document and never linted. Confirmed by signing an edition with `property: { label: 'The Smith place — recurring damp issue', address: '14 Dundas Street West' }` (probe via npx tsx, since deleted): SIGNED, no House Style refusal. TITLE: Gap report — The Smith place — recurring damp issue "issue" is rule one of the lint (houseStyle.ts:68-73) and House Style §7 bans it outright.
findings.why_it_matters: The `<title>` is client-facing: it is the browser tab on the link the editor hands over (GapReport.tsx:130, `api.editionUrl(e.id)`) and it is what most browsers print into the header when the page is saved as PDF. The lint was extended to the footer precisely because "the first render put `op-dp` in the footer" (render.ts:127-131) — the same class, one field over, and this one is an operator-typed free-text field, which is exactly where a banned word gets in.
findings.falsifiable_as: If this were real, an edition signed for a property whose label contains a banned word and whose address is set stores HTML whose `<title>` carries that word, with no HouseStyleRefused thrown — demonstrated above. It would be disproved if `label` were linted somewhere else on the path; grepping `lint(` in render.ts returns five call sites (lines 197, 198, 199, 201, 205, 206) and none reads `property.label` unconditionally.

findings.title: The in-code default group frame still carries the exact wording the design session retracted as a not-accessible claim over not-inspected data.
findings.evidence:
server/src/report/names.ts:60-66 —
  return {
    default: one(block.default) ?? {
      withRoom: 'In {room}, we were not able to cover:',
      withoutRoom: 'We were not able to cover:',
    },
    byReason,
  }

schema/client-names-v1.json, `frames.corrections.notReachedWording`:
  "'we were not able to cover' claimed we tried and were blocked. That is the NOT-ACCESSIBLE claim made over NOT-INSPECTED data — the exact asymmetry Amendment 1 §A3 exists to hold, arriving through the frame instead of through the label. 'we did not cover' is what the record supports."

The correction landed in the JSON (`"withRoom": "In the {room}, we did not cover:"`) and not in the code copy. `grep -rn "were not able to cover" --include=*.ts --include=*.json --include=*.md .` returns the corrected JSON note, this code fallback, and two test fixtures that hardcode the retracted string (server/test/gap-report.test.ts:25, server/test/carried-items.test.ts:501).

The code fallback is reached whenever the shipped file has no `frames` block or its `default` fails the shape check at names.ts:48-51 (`typeof f.withRoom === 'string' && typeof f.withoutRoom === 'string'`) — a renamed key or a typo is enough, and `framesOf` neither warns nor refuses. Malformed `byReason` entries are dropped the same silent way (names.ts:55-58).

The test written to prevent exactly this claim runs only against the shipped file: server/test/render.test.ts:66-73 loads `loadClientNames()` with its default path, so it exercises the JSON and never the fallback. The doctrine scan at server/test/doctrine.test.ts:1885-1897 asserts `file.frames.default` exists — which is the condition under which the fallback never fires — so it cannot see it either.

The frame is client-facing and unlinted-by-design against this: House Style has no rule for it (the words are all permitted), and render.ts:197 lints the frame only for banned vocabulary.
findings.why_it_matters: "We were not able to cover" tells a homeowner we tried and were blocked. The honesty-label asymmetry documented at clientVoice.ts:80-88 and names.ts:220-232 exists because that is the one claim a gap row may not make without a declared reason, and the label for a `not-reached` row stays `not-inspected` while the frame says otherwise — the label is correct and the sentence the client reads is not. This is the repo's own rule 13 ("a fix for a class of wording is tested on the class") landing in the copy that was open at the time; the code copy was never swept.
findings.falsifiable_as: If this were real, deleting or renaming the `frames` key in `schema/client-names-v1.json` and signing an edition produces a document reading "We were not able to cover:" over `not-reached` rows, with no warning, no lint violation, and render.test.ts's not-reached guard still green because it reads the shipped file. It would be disproved if `framesOf` refused a file with no frames block, or if any check asserted the code fallback's wording — neither exists.

finders.note:
Covered: `server/src/report/{render,clientVoice,draft,names,houseStyle,renderGate,binderDraft}.ts`, `server/scripts/binder.ts`, `web/src/pages/GapReport.tsx`, `schema/client-names-v1.json`, `schema/binder-schema-v1.json`, `schema/profiles/baseline-v1.json`, and `prompts/house-style/v001.md`. I imported both committed fixtures into fresh in-memory databases and ran the real paths — import → runAudit → buildDraft → signEdition for the gap report, and binderDraft's buildDraft/renderDraft with binder.ts's own count expressions — so every finding above is quoted from output I produced, not inferred. Probe scripts were deleted; the only untracked file left in the tree, `server/test/_scratch_seed.ts`, was already there.

Two lens questions came back clean and are worth saying so plainly. **"Can an Inferred value reach a client-facing surface labelled as anything stronger?"** — no, because no client-facing surface renders an honesty label at all today. `ClientGroup.label` is computed and stored in the edition's `composition` JSON but `document()` never emits it; the binder draft emits none; and the binder section renderer that would carry `defaultLabel` does not exist (renderGate.ts:70-76 says so and builds the refusal ahead of it). The claim is instead carried implicitly by the frame wording, which is what finding 6 is about. **`renderGate.ts`** is sound: `gate()` is the only constructor of a `GatedValue`, it lints the words, and `blockedSlots` reports both directions.

Things I looked at and did not report. `clientGroups`'s `if (row.status === 'proposed') continue` (clientVoice.ts:426) is unreachable in the render path — `carriedOf` in render.ts:263-287 rebuilds the item with `status: null`, and a proposed row is already withheld upstream in draft.ts:290-296 — but it is defence in depth behind a guard that works, not a live overclaim. `ClientRow.next` still hardcodes `'No action is needed from you.'` (clientVoice.ts:177) for the deferred case, which is the closer the design session deleted from the `deferred` frame as false; it has no reader (draft.ts:271 takes only `composed?.text`), so it is latent rather than live. And on the walk fixture 129 of 208 carried gaps are withheld from the client document for want of a name, with nothing in the document saying so — render.ts:106-113 argues that case explicitly (the omissions are recorded on the edition and the signer owns them), and the editor does surface them at GapReport.tsx:159-174, so I accepted the defence rather than counting it a defect.
