${esc(column.title)}

${groups}${typed}
` }) `groups` and `typed` only. I signed a real edition from the walk fixture and stripped the tags: the delivered document contains no media line anywhere. It is also unreachable from the desk: GapReport.tsx reads `row.media` (the draft row, lines 334-345) and `e.withheld.length` (line 135), never `columns[].media`. No test in server/test references it. And the location it composes is the wrong register — render.ts:250-259: if (!byWhere.has(row.source.where)) byWhere.set(row.source.where, row) return [...byWhere].map(([where, row]) => ({ where, summary: ... })) against server/src/report/draft.ts:67-70: /** Desk display. May name a zone type; never reaches a client. */ where: string /** Client-safe, or null. What the render composes a location from. */ whereLabel: string | null
findings.why_it_matters: Two problems in one object. First, it is dead weight recorded into the immutable edition record — migration 014 says `composition` is "what it was made of", so the edition claims a component the bytes never had. Second, it is a loaded gun: it sits on `EditionColumn` beside `groups` and `typed`, both of which do reach the client, so the obvious next change (render the media line) ships config vocabulary — "the living-space" — into a homeowner's document. That is precisely the defect Verification Discipline rule 8 records as found and fixed by splitting `where` from `whereLabel`; the split was not carried into `mediaLines`. It is also outside the House Style lint at render.ts:194-202, which lints frames, `next`, item names, typed rows, the signature and the address — not this.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real: sign an edition and search the stored `html` for any media summary string — absent — while `report_editions.composition` contains a populated `media` array. Disproved if any consumer renders it; grep for `.media` across server/src/report and web/src finds only `row.media` (the draft-row desk affordance) and the internals of `mediaLines` itself.

findings.title: Every edition records `house_style_version` as a hardcoded string literal that no code derives, hashes, or checks — including in the test that would catch drift.
findings.evidence:
server/src/index.ts:918, inside the sign route:
      clientNames: { version: names.version, hash: names.hash },
      houseStyleVersion: 'house-style/v001',

Note the asymmetry on the two lines: client names carry a version AND a content hash read from the file; house style carries a literal and no hash. migration 014_editions.sql:43-46 introduces both under one comment — "What produced it, so a difference between two editions is explicable" — and declares `house_style_version TEXT NOT NULL` with no hash column beside it.

Nothing reads the file. index.ts imports no prompt loader at all (`grep -n prompts server/src/index.ts` -> no matches). `loadPrompts` (server/src/ai/prompts.ts:62) does load `prompts/house-style/v001.md` and compute its sha256 — that value exists in memory at runtime and is never asked for; `currentPrompt` is only ever called with the nine AI task names.

And the check cannot fail: server/test/render.test.ts:30 and :252 both pass the same literal `'house-style/v001'`.
findings.why_it_matters: prompts/README.md states the rule this is meant to satisfy: "Every artifact records which prompt version produced it" and "Changing a prompt means changing its version." Today an edition's claim about which writing standard produced it is a sentence typed once, not a fact derived from anything. Cut `prompts/house-style/v002.md`, or edit a rule inside `server/src/report/houseStyle.ts` (which is where the lint actually lives), and every subsequent edition still says `house-style/v001` — so "why does this binder read differently from that one", the question §9 says must always be answerable, is answered wrongly and confidently. This is Verification Discipline rule 9 in the repo's own terms: a document asserting a checked state that carries the claim instead of the check, with two sides that cannot disagree.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real: add `prompts/house-style/v002.md`, sign a new edition, and `SELECT house_style_version FROM report_editions` still returns `house-style/v001`; the test suite stays green. Disproved by any code path that reads the prompts directory when signing — index.ts does not import it.

findings.title: The binder schema's AI guard-rails — `neverAI`, `aiMayDraft`, `specificityRule`, `recordFields`, `completeWhen` — are read by no code, on the same slot whose other declaration is enforced by an unforgeable brand.
findings.evidence:
$ grep -rn "neverAI|aiMayDraft|specificityRule|recordFields|completeWhen" --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' server/src server/scripts web/src
(no output — zero hits for all five)

They are live data. schema/binder-schema-v1.json:1113-1122, `s19.reserve-figure`:
  "neverAI": true,
  "outsideHonestyVocabulary": { "why": ..., "renderNote": ... }
One slot, two declarations. The second is enforced by `renderGate.ts`'s branded `GatedValue` — I ran the gate against the shipped schema and both declaring slots clear, so that half demonstrably works. The first is enforced by nothing.

Also s10.concerns (schema lines 878-893):
  "aiMayDraft": ["what-was-observed", "why-it-matters"],
  "neverAI": ["urgency", "planning-cost-range", "recommended-action"],
  "specificityRule": { "isCompletenessRule": true, "requires": ["measurement","cadence","namedEscalationTrigger"], ... }

`specificityRule` even has an implementation — server/src/audit/completeness.ts:219, `watchScheduleShortfall(record, requires)`, headed "§10's specificity rule — a completeness rule, not style advice." Its only callers are in server/test. The schema field it is written against is never read, so `requires` is never supplied from the schema by anything.

The schema loader carries them through (`Slot` has `[key: string]: unknown`, schema.ts:90) — nothing is dropped, and nothing looks.
findings.why_it_matters: `neverAI` is the machine-readable form of CLAUDE.md §9's hardest rule, and the repo's stated enforcement elsewhere is structural — server/test/operating-state.test.ts:155, "has no column a model could write into, which is how 'never AI' is enforced". That argument holds only while the fields do not exist. The moment §10 concerns or the reserve figure gain a writable field, the declaration that was supposed to stop a model is a JSON key with no reader, and nothing fails on contact to say so. The same repo, on the same slot, shows what the enforced version looks like — the contrast is the finding. `renderGate.ts:69-76` states the discipline explicitly: "the guard has to be in place before the temptation."
findings.falsifiable_as: If real: delete `"neverAI": true` from `s19.reserve-figure`, or add `"neverAI"` to any other slot, and nothing in the test suite or the running app changes. Disproved by any reader of those keys — grep across all of server/ and web/ returns none, and no comment anywhere argues the omission is deliberate (unlike, e.g., `lineage.ts`, which documents at length why its file is empty).

findings.title: 34 of the binder schema's 41 slots have no `title`, so the draft meant for an outside reviewer heads them with raw slot ids.
findings.evidence:
server/src/report/binderDraft.ts:155 —
      const title = slot.title ?? slot.id

Counted from the shipped schema: 41 slots, 7 declare `title`, 34 do not. So the fallback is not a fallback — it is the path 83% of the time.

Actual rendered draft.md (real run, walk fixture):
  ### 2. Home dashboard
  **s2.property-summary** ⚑
  **s2.top-items** ⚑
  ...
  ### 15. Maintenance schedule
  **s15.owner-pro-split** ⚑
  **s15.both-realities** ⚑

against the seven that do carry one, in the same document:
  **Shutoff & control map** ⚑
  **Plain-language response procedures** ⚑
  **Findings** ⚑
findings.why_it_matters: This is Verification Discipline rule 7 exactly — "a fallback whose input is always present is not a fallback... Count how often the safe branch fires. If it is zero, the safe branch is decoration; if it is everything, the mechanism is not doing what its name says." The consequence is the same shape as rule 8's recorded instance: internal vocabulary in a document a person outside the repo reads. The draft's purpose is to spend a reviewer's attention well, and a page of `s15.owner-pro-split` spends it on decoding ids. The fix is not in this repo — it is 34 missing `title` keys in the Master-Spec-derived schema — but nothing today reports that they are missing.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real: run `npm run binder` against any visit and count headings matching /^\*\*s\d+\./ — expect 34. Disproved if any of those 34 slots gains a title and the heading changes, which is what makes this a data gap rather than a code bug; but `buildDraft` neither warns nor counts, so the gap is invisible from the output.

findings.title: `itemSeries` says its purpose is "the surface that lets somebody see the break", and the surface it got is a JSON endpoint no screen calls.
findings.evidence:
server/src/audit/itemSeries.ts:5-7 —
 * **The rule was implemented in Increment 3; showing it to a person was not.**
 * `propertyEvidence` already detects §1k.1 supersession and refuses to join
 * across it. This is the surface that lets somebody *see* the break.

380 lines, one route — server/src/index.ts:988, `GET /api/properties/:id/item-series`.

The web app never asks for it:
  $ grep -rn "item-series|itemSeries" web/src
  (no output)
web/src has exactly 13 files; none references it. Comparing every route in index.ts against every path in web/src, five are unreachable from the UI: `/api/operators` (CLI-managed, fine), `GET /api/properties/:id/audit` (the screen re-POSTs instead), `/api/visits/:id/summary`, `/api/house-style/rules`, and this one.
findings.why_it_matters: The module's own justification is that the rule already worked and only the showing was missing. A route that returns raw JSON at a URL the owner would have to type by hand is not the showing — the honest reading is that Increment 4 §4 built the computation and stopped one step short, and the header now records a completed intent that is not complete. Concretely: when `liv.egress` retires and a series breaks, nobody at the desk sees it, which is the exact failure the module was built to prevent.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real: open the app, navigate every screen, and no view shows a cross-visit answer series or a retirement break; the endpoint returns data when curled. Disproved by any component fetching that path — there is none in web/src.

findings.title: `PhotoTileView` calls `useState` after two early returns, so a tile that changes file status between renders crashes the pass screen.
findings.why_it_matters: React throws "Rendered more hooks than during the previous render" and unmounts the tree, which the concierge sees as the pass screen going blank mid-walk — the one screen CLAUDE.md calls "the highest-value hour in the process". It is latent rather than firing today only because the fixtures have no absent or quarantined media, which is the same reason the two early-return branches themselves have never executed. `placeMedia` writes both states routinely on real imports (`server/src/import/media.ts:142-185`).
findings.falsifiable_as: If real: render a tile whose `fileStatus` is `absent`, then re-render the same key with `present` (or the reverse) — React 18 throws and the pass view is replaced by a blank page. Disproved if `photo.fileStatus` can be shown to be immutable for the life of every mounted tile; I could not find a writer that changes `media.file_status` after import, so I am reporting this as a latent violation rather than a live crash.

finders.note:
Covered: read CLAUDE.md and the full Verification-Discipline note; walked every file in server/src (all 60+ modules, reading headers and the load-bearing functions in audit/, report/, import/, engine/, ai/, pass/, plan/, desk/, overlay/), all 15 scripts in server/scripts, all 13 files in web/src, schema/binder-schema-v1.json + profiles + reference, and prompts/. Cross-checked every Express route in index.ts against every path the web app fetches. Mechanically listed exports whose only non-self reference is a test, then read the interesting ones individually. Verified the repo's own quantitative claims where they were checkable (the 28/7/6 profile partition is exact and disjoint; the render gate's "both slots clear" is true — I ran it; the fixture byte and media-kind figures match the manifests). Ran the real pipeline against fixtures/walk-2026-07-31 with HOUSESTEADY_DATA pointed at scratch: import → audit → gap-report draft → signed edition (HTML dumped and read as text) → binder draft, which is how findings 1, 2 and 7 surfaced as observed output rather than as code reading. Temp scripts were written under server/scripts/.tmpaudit and deleted; nothing in the repo was modified.

Not reached: I did not exercise any path that makes a model call (ai/tasks, the queue, the worker, scoring), so the four identification passes, the golden-set machinery and `npm run passes|proposals|score|read|resolve|match` are unaudited beyond reading them — a runner session with a key would be needed. I did not read the 2,238-line maintenance schedule or the 6,130-line class frame as data, only their consumers. I did not attempt the multipart HTTP import route or run the React app in a browser, so finding 9 is reasoned from source rather than observed.

Two things I looked at and deliberately did NOT report, because the code argues them explicitly and the argument holds: the render gate having no renderer behind it yet (renderGate.ts:69-76 makes the "guard before the temptation" case), and `import-export.ts` moving rather than copying media plus its EXDEV trap (both warned about at length in the script header). `sessionPlan.ts`'s `openConcerns: never[]` and `lineage.ts`'s empty-by-design file are likewise documented and correct. Also noted but not reported: `server/test/_probe_field6.ts` and `_scratch_seed.ts` are untracked working-tree leftovers, not committed.

finders.lens: Field 6 seam readiness — the IMPORT path (server/src/import/**, and the two call planners downstream of it)

findings.title: The identification planner decides "is this a still image" from `kind`, never from `mime`, so a Field 6 floorplan/mesh capture (kind `photo`, mime `application/json`) is planned into a vision call.
findings.evidence:
server/src/engine/identify.ts:52  `export const IMAGE_KINDS: readonly string[] = ['photo']`
server/src/engine/identify.ts:261 `    if (m.kind !== null && IMAGE_KINDS.includes(m.kind)) {`
                          `      usable.push(m)`
The row this decides on never carries a mime at all — server/src/ai/tasks/identify.ts:205-214 selects `m.kind, m.owner_kind, …, m.capture_intent, m.file, m.file_status` and no `m.mime`.

Run: I took `fixtures/walk-2026-07-31/housesteady-019fb92d-manifest.json`, appended the two captures exactly as the Field 6 example declares them (`kind: "photo"`, `mime: "application/json"`, `intent: "floorplan"` / `"mesh"`, real bytes and sha256), imported it, and called `planIdentificationCalls(mediaForImport(db, importId), zoneRoutes(db, importId))`:

  batches containing the JSON captures: [ '019fb92d-afd2-7d1b-a537-a5e5ede81965 #1/2' ]
  excluded mediaIds: [ '…: kind `video` is not a still image this p', … x4 video, x2 voice ]

The four videos and two voice notes are excluded by name. The two JSON files are in `batch.media` — the detail-photograph pile.
findings.why_it_matters: `runIdentify` hands every member of the batch straight to `prepareImage` with no per-file guard — server/src/ai/tasks/identify.ts:591-595, `for (const m of [...context, ...detail]) { prepared.push({ … image: await prepareImage(…) }) }`. `prepareImage` throws `ImageRefused('image.unreadable')` on anything sharp cannot decode (server/src/ai/image.ts:126-132). Nothing catches it inside the job, so the throw reaches `abandonOrRetry` (server/src/ai/worker.ts:184-229), which does not classify `ImageRefused` as permanent — the room's job retries three times with backoff (server/src/ai/queue.ts:22-25) and then sits permanently failed. One 8 KB geometry file costs a whole room its identification pass. The repo already ruled the other way, in writing: server/src/pass/thumbs.ts:122-129 — *"Deliberately a mime check rather than a list of media kinds. `media.kind` is open vocabulary … so switching on it would be exactly the exhaustive-list mistake CLAUDE.md §5 warns about."* The `declare what is consumed, never what is skipped` defence in identify.ts's header is sound against a new *kind* (video falls out correctly, as the run shows) and does not reach a new *mime under an existing kind*, which is precisely what Field 6 ships.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real: import any manifest carrying a media of kind `photo` and mime `application/json`, then call `planIdentificationCalls` — the media id appears inside a `batch.media` array and not in `plan.excluded`. Observed exactly that. It would be disproved if the row landed in `plan.excluded` beside the videos, or if `mediaForImport` selected `mime` and something downstream read it — neither is the case. It would also be moot if Field 6 gave these captures a distinct `kind`, but the field team's own example (`manifestpositionexample.json` lines 68-93) sets `kind: "photo"` on both.

findings.title: The other call planner has the same `kind`-only gate, and hands the floorplan JSON to the model as `role: 'subject'` — a thing to identify — which is the exact failure the comment eight lines above it says the role distinction exists to prevent.
findings.evidence:
server/src/engine/assembly.ts:75  `export const CONSUMED_KINDS: readonly string[] = ['photo']`
server/src/engine/assembly.ts:218 `const isConsumed = (kind: string | null): boolean =>`
server/src/engine/assembly.ts:238 `    if (!isConsumed(m.kind)) {`  → pushes to `unconsumed`, otherwise becomes a subject or context
server/src/engine/assembly.ts:83-86 (the comment on `MediaRole`): `" … But it is not itself a thing to identify: a floorplan sketch returning a proposed object called *a drawing of a room* is the failure this distinction exists to avoid."`

Run (same probe import, with the two rows marked `file_status='present'` so absence is not the confound):

  WITH FILES PRESENT — assembly unconsumed: []
  full batch 0: {"index":1,"subjects":[{"mediaId":"media-plan-4","kind":"photo","mime":"application/json","bytes":8412,"fileStatus":"present","file":"…/media-plan-4.json",…,"role":"subject",…},{"mediaId":"media-mesh-5","kind":"photo","mime":"application/json","bytes":41233,"fileStatus":"present"…
findings.why_it_matters: `assembleImport` is not dead code — it is the single source `propertyReadiness` uses to decide whether the property pass may run (server/src/engine/completeness.ts:146, with the comment forbidding a second query for exactly this reason). So the module that is supposed to be the one place "which media belongs to this zone, and what is it for" is answered puts a RoomPlan JSON in the subjects pile with `role: 'subject'`. `mime` is already on the row here (assembly.ts:93, `mime: string | null`) and carried through to `unconsumed` (assembly.ts:240) — it is available and simply not consulted by the gate.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real: call `assembleImport` on an import holding a present media with kind `photo` and mime `application/json`; it appears in `zone.batches[].subjects` with `role: 'subject'` and is absent from `zone.unconsumed`. Observed exactly that. Disproved if `isConsumed` or the role assignment consulted `m.mime`, or if the row appeared in `unconsumed` alongside video and voice.

findings.title: A `capture_intent` value the builder has never met is stored and never surfaced — so `floorplan` and `mesh`, the two words Field 6 adds, arrive completely silently, contradicting both the vocabulary pass's own stated test and migration 022's own comment.
findings.evidence:
server/src/import/vocabulary.ts:238-244 — the entire media block:
  `  // ------------------------------------------------------------------ media`
  `  for (const x of c.media) {`
  `    if (!known(KNOWN.mediaKind, x.kind)) collector.note('media.kind', x.kind, String(x.mediaId))`
  `    if (!known(KNOWN.mediaOwnerKind, x.ownerKind)) {`
  `      collector.note('media.owner.kind', x.ownerKind, String(x.mediaId))`
  `    }`
  `  }`
`captureIntent` is not read here and there is no `KNOWN.captureIntent` (vocabulary.ts:28-48). `server/src/import/report.ts:115-124` groups media `byKind` and `byOwner`; there is no `byIntent`. `grep -rn "intent" web/src` → nothing.

Both sides exercised, on the real walk export:
  walk.media[0].kind = 'thermal'; walk.media[1].intent = 'floorplan'; walk.media[2].intent = 'mesh'; walk.media[3].owner.kind = 'concern'
  terms: [ "pin.flag=fine x6", "event.type=VoiceNoteAdded x2", "event.type=ExportProduced x1", "media.kind=thermal x1", "media.owner.kind=concern x1", "resolution.via=choice x1" ]
  canonical carried the intents? [ 'floorplan', 'mesh' ]
An unknown kind and an unknown owner kind both surface. An unknown intent does not. And on the full import: `the words floorplan/mesh anywhere in the import report: null`.
findings.why_it_matters: vocabulary.ts:19-21 states the standard this fails: *"The test for fail-open is not that unknown words are tolerated — it is that they are tolerated AND surfaced. A silently swallowed word is the same failure as a crash, just slower."* `022_capture_intent.sql:38-42` asserts the behaviour as already true: *"OPEN VOCABULARY, like every other word from the field. A value this build has not met is stored, **reported**, and treated as ordinary."* It is stored and treated as ordinary; it is not reported. Field 6 §2 says *"The intent is what makes them findable — without it a room's geometry arrives as an unlabelled blob among the pictures"*, and on this import path that is exactly what happens: the desk gets no signal that a floorplan or a mesh arrived. They are also counted as photographs in the one breakdown CLAUDE.md §11 insists on — the probe's report showed `byKind: [{"kind":"photo","count":159,"bytes":508435885}…]`, with 49 KB of RoomPlan JSON inside the photograph bytes.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real: put an `intent` value on a media that no build has met, import, and read `validation.unrecognizedTerms` and the whole import report — the word appears nowhere while `media.capture_intent` holds it. Observed exactly that, with `media.kind` and `media.owner.kind` as working controls in the same run. Disproved if any `collector.note('media.intent', …)` existed, or if the report carried a byIntent breakdown.

findings.title: `checkTotals` reconciles only the ten keys it hardcodes, so a total the export declares under any other name is never compared — `totals.videos` is declared by the real walk export and has never been checked by anything.
findings.evidence:
server/src/import/validate.ts:72-83 builds the comparison set as a closed literal:
  `  const actual: Record<string, number> = {`
  `    zones: …, pins: …, canvases: …,`
  `    photos: c.media.filter((x) => x.kind === 'photo').length,`
  `    voiceNotes: c.media.filter((x) => x.kind === 'voice').length,`
  `    notes: …, chats: …, inboxItems: …, mediaFiles: …, mediaBytes: …`
  `  }`
and validate.ts:85 iterates `Object.entries(actual)` — the declared side is only ever read by key lookup (`c.declaredTotals[key]`), so a declared key absent from this literal is unreachable.

Run, on the unmodified walk export (`declared totals: {"zones":8,…,"photos":157,"videos":4,"voiceNotes":2,…}`):
  unmodified                 -> totals checks: []
  totals.videos = 9999       -> totals checks: []
  totals.photos = 9999       -> totals checks: ['totals.mismatch: totals.photos says 9999 but the file actually contains 157.']
`grep -rn "videos" server/src web/src server/test` → no match anywhere in the repo.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the import's arithmetic guard, and it is one-directional: a key the builder expects and the export omits raises `totals.absent`; a key the export declares and the builder does not expect raises nothing. The walk fixture has carried `videos: 4` since 2026-07-31 and no check has ever been able to disagree with it — rule 11b, *a check whose two sides cannot disagree has not been passing*. It matters for Field 6 specifically because the two new captures are counted somewhere by the field app, and whatever key they land under, this reconciliation will ignore it the same way it has ignored `videos`. Adding a `totals.undeclared-key` warning is the two-line fix that makes the next one fail on contact instead of sitting quiet for a year.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real: set any declared total whose key is not one of the ten to a wildly wrong value and run `checkTotals` — zero checks. Observed with `totals.videos = 9999`, against `totals.photos = 9999` as the positive control in the same run. Disproved if the loop iterated the union of declared and actual keys, or if any code anywhere read `totals.videos`.

findings.title: Field 6's own contract document and example call the media array `files[]`; this repo requires `media[]` as a structural section, so if the rename is real every Field 6 export refuses — and the refusal never mentions the word `files`.
findings.evidence:
server/src/import/adapters/v3.ts:38-47 —
  `const REQUIRED_SECTIONS = [`
  `  'session', 'config', 'zones', 'pins', 'media', 'resolutions', 'totals', 'events',`
  `] as const`
Both real exports use `media`: `fixtures/walk-2026-07-31/…manifest.json` top keys are `manifestSchemaVersion, session, zones, pins, inbox, notes, chats, resolutions, media, totals, orphanEvents, events, config`, and `docs/HouseSteady_Manifest-Contract_v3_2026-07-24.md:24` writes `media[] (paths: …)`. The Field 6 additions doc says `files[].position` and *"listed in `files[]` like any photograph"*, and `manifestpositionexample.json:10` emits a top-level `"files": [` with no `media` key.

Run (walk export, `media` renamed to `files`, nothing else changed):
  canonical produced? false
  [{ "code": "structure.missing-section", "severity": "error", "message": "Required top-level section \"media\" is missing.", "detail": { "section": "media" } }]
findings.why_it_matters: The two readings have opposite consequences and nothing in either repo distinguishes them. If `files[]` is field-side terminology for the wire's `media[]` (likely — migration 022's own comment traces the path as `PhotoAdded -> MediaRef -> MediaFileEntryV3`, a field-side type name), Field 6 is genuinely additive and imports clean, as the probe in finding 1 shows. If the array really is renamed, this is not an additive change at all, `manifestSchemaVersion` staying at 3 is wrong, and every Field 6 export refuses. The refusal itself is doctrine-correct — fail closed on structure, loudly, naming the section — but its message says `media` is missing and never says `files` was found instead, so the operator reads it as a truncated file rather than a contract change. CLAUDE.md §2 makes this a stop-and-ask, not a code change: *"Treat the manifest as fixed input. If something about it seems wrong, say so and stop."*
findings.falsifiable_as: If the rename is real: hand this builder any manifest whose media array is named `files` and the import is refused with `structure.missing-section`, nothing written. Observed. If it is not real — the field app still emits `media[]` and only the prose says `files[]` — there is nothing to fix here and the doc wants one word changed. One question to the field team settles it; no code should move before it does.

finders.note:
WHAT I COVERED. Read all thirteen files in server/src/import/**, plus the two downstream call planners (engine/identify.ts, engine/assembly.ts + engine/plan.ts), pass/thumbs.ts, ai/image.ts, ai/worker.ts, ai/queue.ts, the migration set, and doctrine.test.ts's doctrine-1 block. Everything empirical above came from running the real walk export (fixtures/walk-2026-07-31) through `runImport` with the Field 6 additions grafted on exactly as the field team's example declares them, under `npx tsx`; probe files were written into server/test/, run, and deleted (`git status` clean but for the pre-existing `_scratch_seed.ts`).

DIRECT ANSWERS TO THE LENS QUESTIONS.

1. `position` is PRESERVED, not dropped — but only as bytes. `persist.ts:79` writes `raw_manifest: raw, // verbatim, whole, byte-for-byte what arrived`, and `runImport.ts:319` writes the same bytes to `<visitDir>/manifest.json`. My probe confirmed `raw_manifest holds "position": true`. The canonical shape does drop it: `v3.ts:218-238` enumerates media fields one by one and `position` is not among them. That drop is NOT a defect — it is argued and pinned by `doctrine.test.ts:911-929` ("keeps a field the canonical shape does not model"), whose comment states the design: *"The canonical shape is deliberately lossy — it models what the builder needs. That is only safe because the raw stays the record."* Doctrine 1 holds. What does not exist is any notice: I added both an unknown top-level section and a `positioned:false` refusal to a real export and `parseToCanonical` returned zero checks. Nothing in the import path reports that an export carried structure the builder did not read — the vocabulary pass surfaces unknown *values*, never unknown *keys*. I am not filing that as a defect because nothing yet consumes position and CLAUDE.md §15's convention covers it, but it is why the `positioned:false` refusal — the one state the field team says is worth investigating — will reach the desk invisibly until something is built.

2. An unknown `intent` FAILS OPEN and is stored (`persist.ts:224` → `media.capture_intent`, migration 022), and is treated safely as ordinary by `engine/identify.ts:249,292` (an unrecognised word can neither claim context authority nor drop a photograph). It is not counted, not marked unrecognised, and not on the report — finding 3. So: half of fail-open, which the module itself says is the whole failure.

3. `mime: application/json` is handled correctly where mime is actually consulted — `placeMedia` copies and checksums it like any file with no mime assumption (media.ts:131-184), `pass/thumbs.ts:129` returns `not-an-image` cleanly, and `web/src/pass/Decisions.tsx:342` does the same. It is handled wrongly in the two places that decide what a model looks at, both of which gate on `kind` — findings 1 and 2. Media is not assumed to be images broadly; it is assumed by exactly the two modules where the assumption is expensive.

4. WHAT EXISTS TO STORE POSITION: nothing. `media` (001_initial.sql:173-200, extended by 022) has no spatial column. `anchors.x/y` (001_initial.sql:164-165) is `normalized 0-1 relative to the canvas image` — 2D, per-pin, canvas-space, and unrelated to an ARKit world pose; reusing it would be the mistake. `objects` (017) carries `zone_id` and no coordinates. No table exists for zone geometry, so a floorplan or mesh payload has nowhere to go beyond the media row for its file.

5. SMALLEST CHANGE THAT MAKES POSITION SURVIVE WITHOUT BEING READ — four files, six lines, the same additive pattern migration 022 already established:
   (a) `server/src/db/migrations/027_media_position.sql`: `ALTER TABLE media ADD COLUMN position TEXT;` — verbatim JSON, no schema for it.
   (b) `server/src/import/manifest.ts:159` area: `position?: Record<string, unknown>` on `MediaRecord`, beside `intent?`.
   (c) `server/src/import/adapters/canonical.ts:147` area: `position: Record<string, unknown> | null` on `CanonicalMedia`; `server/src/import/adapters/v3.ts:229` area: `position: (x.position ?? null),`.
   (d) `server/src/import/persist.ts:196-237`: add `position` to the INSERT column list and `j(x.position)` to the values — `j` already null-safes (`db/index.ts:85`).
   Storing the object verbatim keeps all three states distinguishable without inventing a vocabulary: an object with `positioned: true`, an object with `positioned: false` plus `why`, and SQL NULL for absent. NULL for absent is the right encoding precisely because absence means inheritance from the container, not a gap. No reader, no branch, nothing downstream changes — and the container-is-positioned-if-any-frame-is rule stays unwritten until something needs it.

WHAT I COULD NOT REACH. I did not run the full 1224-test suite or the typecheck — every claim above is from a targeted run, not from the suite. There is no real Field 6 export in the repo, so every Field 6 observation is against the field team's hand-written example shape grafted onto a real export; if the real export differs (notably on `kind` for the two JSON captures, or on `files` vs `media`), findings 1, 2 and 5 change. I did not exercise `prepareImage` against an actual JSON file on disk — the ImageRefused path is read from the code, not observed, though `sharp().metadata()` on JSON has no other outcome. And I did not audit the field-side repo, which is where the `files[]` question is actually answered.

finders.lens: Field 6 seam readiness — downstream consumers (media batching/grouping, the session-plan return leg, existing position representation, existing ranking machinery)

findings.title: Every vision call in the repo selects media by `kind` alone; `mime` is never read on the model-call path, so a Field 6 floorplan/mesh JSON with kind 'photo' is batched as a detail photograph and kills the whole room's call.
findings.evidence:
server/src/engine/identify.ts:52,261 —
  export const IMAGE_KINDS: readonly string[] = ['photo']
  ...
  if (m.kind !== null && IMAGE_KINDS.includes(m.kind)) {
    usable.push(m)
    continue
  }

The only other filter above it is `if (m.captureIntent === RUN_TRACE)` (line 249). Nothing tests mime, and `mediaForImport` never fetches it — server/src/ai/tasks/identify.ts:205-218:
  `SELECT m.media_id AS mediaId, m.kind AS kind, m.owner_kind ..., m.capture_intent AS captureIntent, m.file AS file, m.file_status AS fileStatus, n.text AS captureNote FROM media m ...`
(no `m.mime`).

All three vision passes go through this one function: identify (ai/tasks/identify.ts:545), pass 1 (ai/tasks/readSurfaces.ts:225 `planIdentificationCalls(media, zoneRoutes(db, importId), { maxPerCall: 1_000_000 })`), pass 3 (ai/tasks/matchComplete.ts:265). The two queue-time passes hardcode the same test in SQL: `AND m.kind = 'photo'` (nameplate.ts:272, routing.ts:220, pinType.ts:183).

Probe — `npx tsx` against the real exported function, three zone-owned rows, kind 'photo', intents null / 'floorplan' / 'mesh':
  batches: [{ zone: 'z1', media: ['m-photo','m-floorplan','m-mesh'], context: [] }]
  excluded: []
  note: "1 calls over 1 zones, 3 detail photographs. ..."

Then `prepareImage()` on a .json file (server/src/ai/image.ts:127):
  threw: ImageRefused | code: image.unreadable | "Could not read …/floorplan.json as an image: Input file contains unsupported image format"

The prepare loops have no per-file try/catch — identify.ts:591-596, readSurfaces.ts:471-476, matchComplete.ts:657-659 all `await prepareImage(...)` straight into an array. The throw is not `ModelCallFailed`, so `abandonOrRetry` (worker.ts:184) treats it as retryable: three attempts, then `failed`.

Contrast, in this same repo: server/src/pass/thumbs.ts:123-129 —
  // Deliberately a mime check rather than a list of media kinds. `media.kind` is
  // open vocabulary … so switching on it would be exactly the exhaustive-list mistake
  const isImage = (m: MediaRow): boolean => (m.mime ?? '').startsWith('image/')
findings.why_it_matters: One non-image file in a zone takes the entire zone's identification, pass-1 read and pass-3 match with it — not one photograph. server/src/ai/worker.ts:160-161 states the opposite property as settled doctrine: "ONE JOB FAILING NEVER TAKES THE REST. §10. A single unreadable file in a 600-photo visit is a normal Tuesday and the other 599 still have work owed." That holds for the per-media tasks and is false for the three batched passes, where the unit of failure is a room. The recorded error names an image format, not "this is not a photograph", so the operator's diagnosis starts in the wrong place. And engine/assembly.ts:83-85 already names this exact outcome as the thing to avoid — "a floorplan sketch returning a proposed object called *a drawing of a room* is the failure this distinction exists to avoid" — but the mechanism it built for that (subject vs context) keys on owner_kind, which a floorplan riding the ordinary photo path does not trip.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real: import an export containing one zone-owned media row with kind 'photo', mime 'application/json' and a JSON file on disk, then run `npm run identify -- --zone <that zone>`. The plan will list it among the detail photographs (not in `excluded`), the job will fail three times, and `ai_jobs.last_error` will read "Input file contains unsupported image format"; no proposals will exist for that zone. If I am wrong, either the plan would put it in `excluded`, or a mime/intent filter would drop it before `prepareImage`, or the prepare loop would catch per file and send the rest. Grep disproves all three: `grep -rn mime server/src/engine server/src/ai` returns nothing on the selection path.

findings.title: The doctrine scan that enforces allow-list-by-kind pins `CONSUMED_KINDS`, which gates nothing that runs, and cannot reach `IMAGE_KINDS` or the three SQL `kind = 'photo'` predicates that gate every real model call.
findings.evidence:
server/test/doctrine.test.ts:2405 —
  const engineSrc = join(serverSrc, 'engine')
server/test/doctrine.test.ts:2453-2466 —
  it('decides consumption by a declared allow-list, never by excluding kinds', () => {
    for (const file of sourceFiles(engineSrc)) { if (isSkipList(codeOf(file))) offenders.push(...) }
    ...
    const assembly = codeOf(join(engineSrc, 'assembly.ts'))
    assert.match(assembly, /CONSUMED_KINDS[^=]*=\s*\[\s*'photo'\s*\]/, ...)
    assert.match(assembly, /CONSUMED_KINDS\.includes\(/, ...)

The scan's own comment (2446-2448) claims reach it does not have:
  * A positive comparison against `'photo'` is caught too, and deliberately: a
  * hardcoded kind test bypasses the declared constant even when it happens to
  * agree with it today.
The detector is /kind\s*[!=]==?\s*['\"](?:video|voice|audio|photo)['\"]|…/ — `[!=]==?` matches `!=`, `!==`, `==`, `===`, and never a single `=`.

`grep -rn "kind = 'photo'" server/src` →
  server/src/ai/tasks/nameplate.ts:272   AND m.kind = 'photo'
  server/src/ai/tasks/pinType.ts:183     AND m.kind = 'photo'
  server/src/ai/tasks/routing.ts:220     AND m.kind = 'photo'
All three are outside `engineSrc`, and all three use a single `=`.

`grep -an "IMAGE_KINDS" server/test/doctrine.test.ts` → no matches. The live gate (engine/identify.ts:52) is unpinned.

And the pinned constant is dead code: `grep -rn "from './assembly.js'|engine/assembly" server/src server/scripts` returns only engine/plan.ts:44 and engine/runRecord.ts:32-33; `grep -rn "propertyReadiness|assembleImport|plannedRecord" server/src/index.ts server/scripts/*.ts` returns nothing. The whole assembly → plan → completeness → runRecord cluster is imported only by server/test/.
findings.why_it_matters: This is why finding 1 would survive a Field 6 fix. A session told to "make the kind rule mime-aware" is pointed by the test suite at `CONSUMED_KINDS` in engine/assembly.ts — a constant whose only readers are tests — and would leave `IMAGE_KINDS` and the three SQL predicates untouched, with a green suite. Two allow-lists of identical content sit in one directory; the scan asserts one exists and never asserts the other agrees with it.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real: change `IMAGE_KINDS` in server/src/engine/identify.ts:52 to `['photo','floorplan']` and run `npm test`. The suite stays green — no scan and no test pins that constant's contents — while every floorplan is now sent to a vision model. Doing the same to `CONSUMED_KINDS` fails doctrine.test.ts:2463. If I am wrong, the first edit would fail something.

findings.title: `planIdentificationCalls` reports intent-excluded photographs as "excluded by kind", and its zero-batch sentence asserts an absence that is false; the per-row `why` reaches no reader outside tests.
findings.evidence:
server/src/engine/identify.ts:330-339 —
    note:
      batches.length === 0
        ? `No calls. ${media.length} media in, none of them a still image reaching a zone — ${excluded.length} excluded by kind, ${unresolved.length} reaching no zone. That is a state, not a pass.`
        : `${batches.length} calls over ${zoneIds.size} zones, ${detailCount} detail photographs. ` + …
          ` ${excluded.length} excluded by kind, ${unresolved.length} reaching no zone` + …

But line 249-259 excludes on intent, not kind, and pushes `kind: m.kind` (which is 'photo') onto the row.

The only non-test consumer is server/scripts/identify.ts:203-208 —
  if (plan.excluded.length > 0) {
    const byKind = new Map<string, number>()
    for (const e of plan.excluded) byKind.set(e.kind ?? '(no kind)', (byKind.get(e.kind ?? '(no kind)') ?? 0) + 1)
    console.log(`\n  Excluded by kind: ${[...byKind].map(([k, n]) => `${n} ${k}`).join(', ')}`)
  }
  for (const u of plan.unresolved) console.log(`  Unresolved: ${u.mediaId} — ${u.why}`)
`why` is printed for `unresolved` and never for `excluded`. `grep -rn '\.excluded' --include=*.ts` outside tests returns only this block and `ai/tasks/identify.ts:369  excluded: plan.excluded.length` (a bare count on QueuedIdentification).

Probe output, one ordinary photo + one run-trace photo + one video in one zone:
  NOTE: "… 2 excluded by kind, 0 reaching no zone."
  what scripts/identify.ts prints -> Excluded by kind: 1 photo, 1 video
  the why nobody prints: ['t1: marked `run-trace`, which follows a line across rooms. It fi…', 'v1: kind `video` is not a still image…']

Zone whose only media is a run-trace:
  batches: 0 | note: "No calls. 1 media in, none of them a still image reaching a zone — 1 excluded by kind, 0 reaching no zone."
findings.why_it_matters: "Excluded by kind: 1 photo" is a sentence a person reads before paying for a run, and it is wrong twice — the exclusion was not by kind, and the run-trace `why` (the careful sentence about a trace crossing rooms, written for #133) is the one thing that would explain it. The zero-batch line goes further and states a falsehood: the file *is* a still image and it *did* reach a zone. Field 6 makes this the normal case rather than the edge — if floorplan/mesh are excluded by intent the same way, every one of them will be reported as a photograph excluded by kind.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real: import an export with any media carrying `intent: "run-trace"` and run `npm run identify`. The summary line names it as excluded by kind while `media.kind` is 'photo', and its `why` appears nowhere in the output. If I am wrong, the script would print the exclusion reason, or the row would carry a kind other than 'photo'.

findings.title: `capture_intent` is the only vocabulary field from the manifest that is never checked for unrecognised values, contradicting two comments that say it is reported.
findings.evidence:
server/src/import/vocabulary.ts:239-244 —
  for (const x of c.media) {
    if (!known(KNOWN.mediaKind, x.kind)) collector.note('media.kind', x.kind, String(x.mediaId))
    if (!known(KNOWN.mediaOwnerKind, x.ownerKind)) {
      collector.note('media.owner.kind', x.ownerKind, String(x.mediaId))
    }
  }
No `media.intent`. `KNOWN` (lines 28-47) declares no intent list at all.

The field is read (import/adapters/v3.ts:229 `captureIntent: str(x.intent)`) and written (import/persist.ts:224). `grep -rn "capture_intent|captureIntent" --include=*.ts` gives every consumer: canonical.ts:147, v3.ts:229, persist.ts:198,224, ai/tasks/identify.ts:211 (the SELECT), engine/identify.ts:92,249,292. Nothing in import/report.ts, nothing in pass/read.ts, nothing in web/.

The migration that added it claims otherwise — server/src/db/migrations/022_capture_intent.sql:37-39:
  -- OPEN VOCABULARY, like every other word from the field. A value this build has
  -- not met is stored, reported, and treated as ordinary — never a reason to
  -- refuse a row.
And server/src/engine/operatingState.ts:47-50 cites it as an established pattern:
  * A state this build has not met is stored, displayed and counted as
  * unrecognised. … the same safety property `surface` and `captureIntent` have
`surface` really does have it — engine/surfaces.ts:60-64 returns `{ surface, recognised }` and readSurfaces.ts:326 collects `unknownSurfaces`. `captureIntent` has no `recognised` computation anywhere.
findings.why_it_matters: The behavioural half of fail-open is honoured (an unknown intent is treated as ordinary and cannot claim context authority). The reporting half is not, and reporting is the half doctrine 7 is actually about — "preserve, display, count, mark unrecognised". Field 6's `floorplan` and `mesh` are precisely words this build has not met; today's `pan` already is one. Each will be imported and treated as an ordinary detail photograph with no line anywhere saying an unmet intent arrived, so the first signal will be finding 1's failure rather than a vocabulary row on the import report.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real: import a manifest whose media carry `"intent": "floorplan"` and open the import report. The unrecognised-terms table will list nothing about intent, while a media row with `"kind": "lidar"` in the same file does produce a `media.kind` row. If I am wrong, `collector.note('media.intent', …)` would exist in vocabulary.ts.

findings.title: Pass 1 and pass 3 discard `excluded` and `unresolved` from the plan they build on, so neither has any path to report what it did not send.
findings.evidence:
server/src/ai/tasks/readSurfaces.ts:225-258 — planSurfaceReads calls the shared planner and keeps only the batches:
  const plan = planIdentificationCalls(media, zoneRoutes(db, importId), { maxPerCall: 1_000_000 })
  …
  return {
    batches,
    canvasDropped,
    note: batches.length === 0
      ? `No pass-1 calls. Nothing in this import is a detail photograph reaching a zone.`
      : `${batches.length} calls over … ${canvasDropped} canvas frame(s) deliberately not sent …`,
  }
`plan.excluded` and `plan.unresolved` are referenced nowhere in the function, and `QueuedRead` (readSurfaces.ts:155-160) is `{ jobs, zones, photographs, note }` — no field for them.

Same in pass 3 — server/src/ai/tasks/matchComplete.ts:249-254:
  export interface MatchPlan {
    batches: MatchBatch[]
    withScaffold: number
    withoutScaffold: number
    note: string

and its zero-batch note (line 298): 'No calls. Nothing in this import is a still image reaching a zone.'

`grep -n excluded server/scripts/read.ts server/scripts/match.ts server/scripts/passes.ts` → no output. Only `scripts/identify.ts` prints anything, and finding 3 covers what it prints.
findings.why_it_matters: Doctrine 6 — never drop anything silently — and it is dropped at the seam where Field 6 lands. Identification at least emits a (mislabelled) count; the read and match passes emit nothing at all, so a video, a voice note, an unanchored pin's photographs or a floorplan is invisible to the two passes that produce the nameplate readings and the object inventory. The zero-batch sentences in both files repeat identification's false absence: "Nothing in this import is a detail photograph reaching a zone" is stated even when photographs reached zones and were excluded for a reason the caller is never shown.
findings.falsifiable_as: If real: run `npm run read` on the walk fixture (157 photo, 4 video, 2 voice) and the output will not mention the 4 video or 2 voice rows anywhere; `npm run identify` on the same import does mention them. If I am wrong, `planSurfaceReads`'s return type would carry the excluded rows, or scripts/read.ts would print them.

findings.title: `priorUnitPhoto` — the one field in the session plan whose purpose is re-photographing from the same position — returns the most recent photograph on the pin, which its own contract forbids; the test and the doctrine scan guarding it cannot currently fail.
findings.evidence:
server/src/plan/sessionPlan.ts:413-428 —
    const candidates = evidence.graph.lineage(pin.componentType!).flatMap((t) => units.get(t) ?? [])
    let priorUnitPhoto: PlanTypedPin['priorUnitPhoto'] = null
    for (const itemId of candidates) {
      const resolution = evidence.pinResolutions.get(pin.pinId)?.get(itemId)
      if (resolution?.kind !== 'satisfied') continue
      const media = db
        .prepare(
          `SELECT m.media_id, m.captured_at FROM media m JOIN imports i ON i.id = m.import_id
            WHERE i.property_id = ? AND m.owner_pin_id = ? ORDER BY m.captured_at DESC LIMIT 1`,
        )
        .get(propertyId, pin.pinId) as { media_id: string; captured_at: string | null } | undefined
The query does not mention `itemId` — it is identical on every iteration of the loop it sits inside, and returns the newest pin-owned photograph whatever satisfied the item.

docs/HouseSteady_Binder-Builder_Session-Plan-v0_Contract_2026-07-31.md §6:
  "**There is deliberately no fallback to \"the most recent photo on this pin.\"** The two canonical
   photographs stay distinct — the **unit shot** (condition over time) and the **nameplate shot**
   (identity and age evidence, Manifest Contract §7b) — and inventing a comparison position from an
   arbitrary photograph would conflate them. A scan holds it."

The scan (server/test/doctrine.test.ts:2071-2077) is a regex over source text:
    const resolve = plan.slice(plan.indexOf('const candidates'), plan.indexOf('return {\n      pinId'))
    assert.match(resolve, /candidates/, 'the item ids come from the config')
    assert.ok(!/\?\?\s*media\b|else\s*\{[^}]*most recent/i.test(resolve), 'no fallback to an arbitrary photograph …')
Neither branch of that regex describes the code above; it asserts the absence of an `??` and of a literal comment.

The behavioural test (server/test/session-plan.test.ts:315-323) asserts the loop body never runs:
    assert.equal(p.typedPins.every((o) => o.priorUnitPhoto === null), true)
and the contract's own §6 explains why it cannot: "Field config **v1.2.1** *(what this repo holds)* | **0**" `.unit` items. Master v1.11 declares 27.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the artifact that rides back into the field, and this is the field in it that exists so the same object is framed the same way month to month. On the first config carrying `.unit` items the plan will start sending a mediaId — and on any pin that has both a unit shot and a nameplate shot, the newer one wins, which is usually the nameplate: exactly the conflation §6 forbids, arriving in the payload the contract calls "the one place a wrong claim reaches a reader who never opens this document." Neither guard can announce the change, because both are idle for the reason the contract states (Verification Discipline rules 11 and 16 — a check whose distinguishing input is never present, and a query whose output does not depend on what it checks).
findings.falsifiable_as: If real: seed a pin with two photographs — an older one and a newer nameplate shot — under a config that declares a `.unit` item resolved satisfied for that pin, and `buildSessionPlan` returns `priorUnitPhoto.mediaId` = the newer nameplate shot. If I am wrong, the query would constrain on the item's evidence, or on capture role, and would differ between iterations of the `candidates` loop; it does not — `itemId` appears only in the recorded output, never in the WHERE clause.

finders.note:
WHAT I COVERED. Every consumer that batches or groups media, traced to the line that selects: engine/identify.ts (the single planner all three vision passes share), ai/tasks/identify.ts, readSurfaces.ts, matchComplete.ts, nameplate.ts, routing.ts, pinType.ts, ai/image.ts, ai/worker.ts + queue.ts (failure handling), engine/assembly.ts + plan.ts + completeness.ts + runRecord.ts, import/vocabulary.ts + report.ts, pass/thumbs.ts, plan/sessionPlan.ts, overlay/store.ts, engine/surfaces.ts, engine/reviewQueue.ts. Docs read: CLAUDE.md, the Verification Discipline note, the Session Plan v0 contract in full, migration 022. I ran the real exported functions under tsx rather than reasoning from the source (probes in the scratchpad), and read the walk fixture's manifest directly.

WHERE MEDIA IS SELECTED FOR A MODEL CALL — the exact line. server/src/engine/identify.ts:261, `if (m.kind !== null && IMAGE_KINDS.includes(m.kind))`. It filters on **kind**. It filters on **intent** only at line 249 and only for the literal `run-trace`. It never filters on **mime**, and mime is not even fetched (ai/tasks/identify.ts:205-218). A floorplan/mesh JSON at kind 'photo' is batched as a detail photograph and reaches `prepareImage`, which throws `ImageRefused` and takes the whole zone-batch job down. Finding 1.

DOES THE SESSION PLAN NEED `position`? Structurally, one field does and it is `typedPins[].priorUnitPhoto` — contract §6's whole argument is *"nothing in the field app can enforce consistent framing unaided and at hour three the concierge will not recall the angle"*, and `sections.priorUnitPhotographs`'s own sentence (sessionPlan.ts:765-768) is *"so the same object is photographed from the same position rather than differently every month."* Today it carries `{ mediaId, capturedAt, itemId }` — a picture to look at, no pose. Nothing else in the plan reads or needs position: `zones[]` is attributes, `carriedGaps[]` is item ids and dates, `monitorsDue`/`comparisonPositionsDue` are id pairs, `openConcerns` is `never[]`. Whether the field wants a pose there is the field session's call and a `planSchemaVersion`-additive question under §12 — I am reporting the seam, not proposing the field. What I did find is that the field is already wrong about *which photograph* (finding 6).

IS A PHOTOGRAPH'S LOCATION REPRESENTED ANYWHERE? No — not a photograph's. Two things carry a location and both are a **pin's**, both 2D, both normalised against a canvas image:
 · `anchors` (migrations/001_initial.sql:159-171; canonical.ts:121-128) — `{anchorId, pinId, canvasId, x, y}`, field-minted, bounds-warned at import/integrity.ts:182-199.
 · the `place` overlay (overlay/store.ts:71-78, 305-340) — the desk's own placement, same `{canvasId, x, y}` shape plus required `evidence` naming what the position was read from.
The relation to a 3D pose is that there isn't one. A canvas anchor answers *where on this picture is the marker*; an ARKit pose answers *where in the room was the camera*. The anchor has no camera, no depth, no frame of reference beyond one image, and `media` has no spatial column at all. `PlaceValue` also cannot be widened quietly: overlay/store.ts:327-334 hard-refuses anything outside [0,1] and requires a `canvasId` that resolves in `canvases`, so a pose would be a new overlay kind, not a wider `place`.

RANKING MACHINERY TO REUSE FOR "closest frame wins by surface.distance". Yes, and it is `adjudicateManufacturer` in server/src/engine/surfaces.ts:180-236. It is the repo's worked answer to *competing claims about one fact*, and its shape is the one a distance ranking needs: it returns `{ asserted, supportedBy, claims, competing, why }`; losers are **retained, not deleted** ("Losing is a position in a list, not an absence from it", surfaces.ts:176-178, written against Register #121 where one column with room for one answer let the last write win); and a tie **asserts nothing** rather than picking arbitrarily (`distinct.length > 1` → `asserted: null`). A naive `frames.sort(byDistance)[0]` reproduces exactly the bug that function exists to prevent. The other sorts I checked are not this shape and should not be reused: engine/identify.ts:279-280 (`inWalkOrder` — determinism, not preference), engine/assembly.ts:319-341 (`stableByCapturedAt`), engine/reviewQueue.ts:127-130 (label frequency), engine/lookup.ts:132-145 (`specificity: unit|line|family|none` — a *specificity* ladder for product strings, closer in spirit but about text, not geometry). Note also that `surfaces.ts` gives the safety property Field 6 will want verbatim: an unrecognised surface is not `nameplate`, so a word nobody has met cannot acquire authority — the same argument applies to an unrecognised intent and a missing `distance`.

TWO PARALLEL BATCHERS, ONE OF THEM DEAD. `engine/assembly.ts` + `plan.ts` + `completeness.ts` + `runRecord.ts` implement the same resolve-to-zone / subject-vs-context / split-into-batches logic as `engine/identify.ts`, with different rules — assembly derives role from `owner_kind` alone (plan.ts:203-221) and has never heard of `capture_intent`, so it would call a `room-shot` a subject and a `run-trace` an ordinary photograph.
